posts.title: Relics from a Dragon Time
posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 1:
Relics from a Dragon Time 
Part 1
   -14,000 SD*
   Io the Ninefold Dragon soared over Oerth.
   They looked down upon it for one last time.
   Life had irrevocably changed. What had once been a paradise of banquets, magic and laughter had grown dark.
   Avarice had come to Oerth.
   And jealousy. And vanity.
   The Draconians had broken themselves.
   Io sailed across the great continent Oerik*,* once a United Utopia, but now a reminder of what had been lost.
  Here was the place where Bahamut the Platinum dragon and Tiamat the Chromatic dragon sundered themselves into emnity eternal.
   Dragons became fixed, rigid. Trapped in singular form.White remained white. Silver remained silver. 
    Io had failed to reconnect the rift.
   Now they were the Ninefold Dragon when once they were but one. 
   Nine for nine schisms.
   The empire was now empires.
   And so much had been lost.
   Io hardly saw a single dragon. The land swept out before them in brown, green and blue.
 * Suel date.
** Most of the names used in this history are those used by the current Common tongue. The continent Oerik was named by the Oeridians who migrated into the Flanaess (Eastern Oerik) some 1100 years ago. Prior names of Oerik include Sylv, Kazebruk, Jonphur and Xagra. See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book: 1
Relics from a Dragon Time 
Part 2
-20,000 SD
     The Dragon Schism, whereby the dragon families attempted to wrest full control of the Empires, was a major disruption on Oerth.  Many worlds were interconnected by portals that allowed empires to rule different planets simultaneously.  The effect on Oerth was profound, because the vacuum created by the deaths of countless dragons and dracoforms in the horrific wars allowed new types of intelligent life to emerge out from the shadows.
   The first elves, or Olve, as they called themselves had arrived on Oerth over a thousand years earlier as slave races for the dragons, but during the Schism the Olve liberated themselves, first the Tuatha de Dannan, who discovered and joined with the Fey dimension, then later the lesser Olve, tied closer to Oerth.
   At the final end, the various dragon empires had disintegrated. and the dragons themselves had become scarse. Their leaders fled to the Outer Planes and many worlds grew wild and free.  The elves proliferated, relics left behind in the apocalypse, and their story is next... See less

posts.title: Relics of a Dragon Time
posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book:1
Relics of a Dragon Time 
Part 3
Olve
  Olve inherited the world.  
  Sprites, pixies, griggs and satyrs frolicked in the meadows, forests and thickets. 
 Thousands of years pass.
   Olve deep in the mysteries of Fey became the Grey elves.  Olve on the coast became enamoured of pearls and other shiny things.  They develop sailing and settle on many islands across the ocean.  Other elves attempted to take to the mountains and mine for beautiful gems and minerals, but most hated being underground for long and didn't like to work. They returned to the lowlands.
    In another world, Olve discovered a different demi-human, the dwarves.Olve brought into Oerik a few clans, magically charmed to be docile and servile.The dwarves seemed to like dirty and ugly things  and thrived in dark places, because they were inferior and lowly creations, not like the transcendent Olve lovingly carved by the greatest Dragons.
 Many dwarves were sent into the mountains to mine beautiful stones for the elves.  
   Although there were a few fell monsters, loose relics of the Dragon Age, that roamed the empty places, the beautiful creations, the centaurs, unicorns, and pegasi abounded.  It was a good time to be Olve. See less

posts.title: Relics From a Dragon Time
posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 1
Relics From a Dragon Time 
Part 4
Dwur!
-12,000 SD
 Dwarves were stupid!
   Why had the dragons ever bothered creating them? The dwarves had been enchanted slaves of the elves for several thousand years now and the elven magic, wrapped in the Fey Mysteries, were too strong for the dwarves natural resistance to overcome.
   Delphine used her dwarves to dig into the dirt under the mountains to find bright and beautiful things for her. Is that what the dwarves were for? Did the dragons create them to be thralls?
   She wasn't the only one using the dwarves in this way. Really, there wasn't much else that dwarves were good for. Their cooking was atrocious, they were slow and clumsy, physically and mentally, their art was obvious and very simple, so no point employing them for that, and they were boring company. And it was pathetic that Olve magic enslaved them so easily. Dwarves had no dignity either.
   Yet, there were a few dwarves who resisted, a tiny number. In fact, only a few hundred dwarves in each generation managed to break the charms.
   Why? Not because they grew a spine, or because their esteem demanded freedom. Darlene scoffed, no!
   It was base avarice. These few dwarves fell under the spell of gold fever instead of Olve. She heard stories that these degenerates tunneled deep into the Underdark far away from elvish eyes.
    Sages spoke of the deep dwarves forming sinister cults that worshipped the slithering creatures of the darkness. Elder Things not Dragon, cast-offs from the old empires.
   Darlene shuddered. Thank the Dragons that she was Olve!
                           *****
   Moradin felt alone.
    He was born differently, a dwur that could think for himself. He had never been affected by elvish magic and nor was he struck with gold fever. Alone amongst the dwur, he grew up independent and angry, unable to relate to the charmed dwarves all about him, hiding from the elves and stealing from them as he needed to survive. He was achingly lonely. Why had the Dragons made him? Why give him a fierce intelligence and a steely will if all he could be was a vagabond, a rutterkin? 
   He should be more. 
   He should be a leader for his people.
   He saw an aura about them, and he felt their pain. 
   The dwur were treated as shells, bodies with no brains.
   Moradin knew that their minds were clever. Their will was staunch.
   They couldn't help the magic that suppressed it. Moradin would find a way to break it.
   He would be more.
   The dwur would be free.
   And their overlords would pay! See less

posts.title: Relics from a Dragon Time
posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 1
Relics from a Dragon Time 
Part 5
Oerth
    Io had the cosmos, but the Ninefold Dragon felt drawn to Oerth, and Oerik in particular.
 Oerik was a large continent divided by the great spine of the Barrier Peaks, the Crystalmists and the Hellfurnaces. Various lesser ranges broke up long forests, grasslands and fertile valleys. This was not particularly different to any of the other continents that dotted Oerth. Perhaps Io saw the loss and scars, for some of the greatest upheavals happened there.
   South of Eastern Oerik were two continents, 
one small and one large, called today Hepmonaland and Melavi. Places of jungle and swamp, many secrets lurked within, shielded from Io's aerial view.
East of Eastern Oerik, within the Solnor sea was a large island called Kodge Land, and a little further over, the continent known as Mystara.  
Continuing a long way east, past Mystara across the Mystaran Ocean are two sister continents, one to the north called Kingsland, or C'mu N'eir.  The Tuatha de Dannan lived here. South is a larger land known as Adarus.  
   Io glided South East. There they were, the Lost Lands, an even bigger emotional wrench than Oerik. Mysterious magic, terrible monsters and strange intelligent beings, further cast offs beyond Io's understanding, lurked in this terrible land.
Io returned to Oerik, gliding into the western parts. It was definitely dryer, and the Olve-relics were scarce. Draco Forms predominated. Did these simpler life-forms still think that the Empires existed?
   Io continued west, across the foamy wastes of the enormous Dramidj Ocean, the tiny central islands, and now, with the great peaks of volcanoes rising out of the water like the bones of the Dragon Emperors, great Kara-Tur, a super continent that stretched north into the arctic and south into the Antarctic...
   Vast Oerth. Precious Oerth. 
   The Cast-offs, the Relics lay across the world, chaotic and threatening, for Io couldn't understand them, and to Olve and Dwur, he was only a shadow on the sun. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 6
Get out of the Mud, for the Sun is sharp.
   Moradin from The Book of the Sombre. Chapter 13, verse 7.
   Moradin was born in the Western Crystalmists around 11,500 years ago.  He was not affected by the elvish enchantments that enslaved most dwarves.  Wise, strong and intelligent, he despaired of the wrongs done to his people.  He tried to rouse his fellows to revolution but they were "affixed to servitude like iron" (Chapter 11 Verse 9).  Eventually he retreated into the depths of the Oerth following the Gold lusted dwarves.  These dwarves were free but rapacious and cruel.  They fought over the control of gold and gem deposits and were willing to stir the dragons from their slumber if it could lead to more wealth.  
   Moradin had little interest in gold (some interest admittedly, he was a dwarf after all!) and focussed on mining useful metals.  He created an alloy of iron and mithril that glowed with the natural magic of the Underdark.  With this alloy he made a great hammer and forge.  Some of the greedy dwarves agreed to be armed by Moradin's in order to free their brethren, but when fully equipped, they reneged and made war on the goblinoids who dwelt near great seams of platinum and gold. The goblins, bugbears, ogres and norkers counted amongst them powerful individuals that included barbarians and warlocks.  Disrupted from their homeland, and full of fury, they poured out of the tunnels and reached the surface, raiding the elves and faerie peoples for the first time.
Moradin was forced to fight against them as he retreated back to the upper mines.  The enchanted dwarves had enough self awareness to defend themselves from the rampaging norkers and goblins but their weapons and armour were crude.  Moradin was able to use his magical forge to create strong mail.  When the charmed dwarves put on the mithril alloy armour their minds cleared and they were free.  Moradin had given them their souls. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1
Part 7
Mushrooms begin in the dark, but they do quest the light.
Dwulf the Prophet. Book of the Sombre, Chapter 17 verse 11.
The goblinoids harried the surface folk for decades.  Elves, who had little use for combat in general life now had plenty of time to hone their skills with bow and sword.  As well as goblins, kobolds, norkers and ogres, hostile dwarves emerged from the mountains and they were fearsome indeed with their magical arms.  Moradin led his people with wisdom but strength also.  After about sixty years of fighting the goblinoids were scattered but not eradicated.  Their fast growth rate meant a couple of dozen hidden goblins could soon become a thousand.The dwarves were not so easily moved.
   Corellon Larethian was a young elf warrior, lithe, strong, clever and magically gifted who had become the best Archer of all the elves. When he Dwarven armies of Moradin, attired in ring mail and heavily armed, marched through the high countries into the forests of Celadon, Corellon and his company were waiting. The elves felled many dwarves with arrows fired within the trees.  It was Anger that had mostly motivated Moradin: he sought revenge on his elvish enemies, but now, in the forest that made him feel claustrophobic and disoriented, he saw little point in pushing through. The dwarves had captured  chains of hills and mountains, and that was the land they most wanted. The dwur had gained their liberty, they had lifted themselves out of the dirt and into the daylight.  The sun was sharp with arrows and it was time to seek shade.
   No accurate conversation has been recorded between Moradin the Soul Forger and Corellon  Larethian. Elvish and Dwarven tales tell different stories, but we know a truce was reached .The dwarves were freed from their enchanted thraldom, and in return there was an acceptance that revenge upon the elves was not to be sought. but for their mutual benefit, and in the face of the common goblinoid enemy that were forever gathering power in the shadows, the two peoples agreed to trade with each other and to respect each other's territories. It didn't mean they had to like each other but Corellon was a fair and honest leader and so was Moradin. 
To this day large conflicts between dwarves and elves are almost unknown, partly in honour of a legendary agreement and partly because both always seem to have much more implacable foes to deal with... See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 8
The Illithids gazed upon Oerth. The tentacled, robed, bipedal octopoids were an ancient race, twisted by the Elder gods from corrupt ritual couplings of Aboleth and Krakens. When dragons ruled the Oerth, the Illithids had psionically wandered amongst the stars. It is also  thought that these dangerous beings developed the magic used in dimensional gates that allowed interstellar travel across the galaxy.  
   Over thousands of years, the Illithids inhabited planets of lesser creatures,usually non intelligent, and sucked their meagre minds. The banal, rubbery taste failed to sate their hunger: they needed and wanted tastier thoughts. Using dimensional gates, psionics and magic combined, they looked upon the sentient worlds. Dragons were too formidable and numerous on many of these and so it was necessary to widen the search.  Across the vastness of space they travelled, gating into worlds deep within the Underdark, or sojourning upon the surface on moonless nights, for the fiery orbs of space would burn their sensitive tentacle- probes.  Eventually they scried the elves of Oerth... See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 9
When an occasional elf disappeared from the Vesve forest, it was sad for the families but no one was really alerted to what was actually happening,. After all, there were baleful things in the woods. So it was that the alien abductions went on wholly unnoticed at first.  
   Tristram and Isolde, two young wood elven newlyweds, found themselves all at once in a stony bloodstained cell in the darkness. The cell was cold , hard and smelled. A  pool of blood glistened on the floor with parts of a sheep soaking in it. After untold hours, two lurching, tentacled horrors in grey robes came into the cell and grabbed Isolde. Tristram fought back but a psionic blast smashed him hard into the back wall. 
Isolde appeared back in the cell two days later, but Tristram found that her eyes were glazed over, and she did not utter a word or seem to recognise Tristram. 
Tristram was next,. Faint from a lack of food and water, and nursing a large lump on his head, Tristram was unable to resist when the monstrous beings returned for him.He was placed onto a bloody slab and his arms and legs were bound up with thick lead lined ropes that smelt of rotten cabbage. There was a brief pause and Tristram was left alone with his fears. But not for too long. At last came the thud, thud of heavy footsteps accompanied by a hissing, gurgling gargle. A huge tentacled pale violet head leered down at him  its tentacle-probes twitching with excitement... See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 10
I would like to say Tristram the wood elf was able to escape the ropes that bound him and then slew the hideous Illithid.  Alas...
   According to the Illithid Researchers of Exquisite Cuisine, sheep and cow minds tasted like rubbery gruel and only rated 2 on the Sensation Scale, dwarves tasted like powdery biscuits and merited a 4, while elven brains were succulent like chocolate souffle and champagne, rich and decadent, rating a solid 9 but  gave the devourer dizzy spells and a queasy stomach afterwards  Hallucinatory episodes were also not uncommon, usually involving flowery meadows and laughing tiny people., So, good for small gatherings but not great for regular consumption. Seeking food more nutritious, and still delicious, the Mind Flayer Researchers of Exquisite Cuisine gated from world to world. 
 11,000 years ago they found a system of planets filled with intelligent short lived bipeds.  They are today known as "humans.". Thousands were collected over the following decades and the captives were divided by their general appearance, size, shape and hair colour, then bred and cross bred and mixed and sorted and spliced and engineered, all with the goal of discovering new taste sensations by the Researchers. Many  flavoursome delicacies were created in their laboratories and breeding pens, which brought fame and wealth to the Researchers and much relish and delicate enjoyment for the Illithids.  Roast beef, creme brulee, venison, cognac and peacock; human minds were capable of such tasty sensations. The brains were combined and recombined to intensify the complexity and flavour notes.
   Humans had another string to their bow, they bred rapidly and were efficient labourers, scribes and artisans. Clever and adaptable. what a useful commodity they were! See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 11
   What was Eastern Oerik like 10,200 years ago?  No humans, elves predominate, but their slow reproduction rate means there are no more than a million elves on this part of the continent. They are beginning to divide into different groups.  
Elves in the dense woodlands who spend much time practising the Fey mysteries and practice great magicks are becoming the Grey elves; those of the forests who prefer creating music and poetry while cavorting with dryads and nymphs and satyres become the sylvan elves. 
 Some elves build villages and gardens and trade with the dwarves (who number about 250,000).  They tend to be a little more organised than their brethren and have wide interests.  They are destined to become the High elves.
   Many wild beasts roam the lands.  Lamia, Griffons and hippogriffs are numerous.  Dragons are still sorting out their differences in far away places, but a handful bronze, silver and Greyhawk dragons are taking an interest in high elf society.and use their influence to order it and help to create permanent structures.
 Many deer, boar, horses and aurochs wander at will and they make the lions share of prey for the monsters, big cats and wolves.  The rivers are perilous, filled with enormous fish, and the lakes are mostly unexplored. 
The south lands destined to become the Bright Desert are fertile grass and woodlands, the Agrar Hills nestle snugly upon the future Rift Canyon, and the Land of Black Ice is for now just mundane tundra. 
   The sea is empty of pirates, the land empty of bandits, the Cairn hills lay undisturbed, keeping their secrets. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 12
   Winding around the Material Plane, , connecting the Astral Plane with the Ethereal, the Fey with the Shadow and caressing the Inner Planes is the mysterious Plane of the Arcane. There is no known way of entering and exiting the plane, or what would be needed to bring to the Plane in order to survive.  Its invisible nature and secret egress mean that very few even know of its existence; possibly there is currently no one extant on Oerth that does, but it plays an important role in limiting magical power.
   The Arcane Plane is an infinite single layer, but the layer is broken into huge bands of different colours.*  As the Plane drifts and twirls about in its its erratic way, different bands touch different parts of the Prime Material and it is these bands that change the power of magic in the region. In 623 CY,  the band around Oerth and it's nearby systems allow mages to basically only cast up to 9th Level Spells.  Back 10,200 years ago a different coloured band touched Oerth.
   Intelligent, literate beings would often know a spell or two.  Elves when attacking would often cast a Magic Missile before reverting to regular arrows.  Magic weapons and armour were easier and cheaper to make than now, and those special individuals devoted to studying the magical arts could reach enormous power.    
 if characters of the Common era were to travel back in time, they would find super powered elves teleporting from place to place, great magical offensive spells that could  obliterate several square miles, and warriors great as demi gods.  Dwarves did not cast conventional spells but were able to enchant items in  mystical ways. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 13
 10,200 years ago, Dwurin Sourshadow, the Dwarven Merchant of Fine Wares, was going for a stroll at twilight just outside the High elven town of Fairfeather near the Fals river in what was then lush woodland.* He had had a good run in Fairfeather, and his pouch clinked with coin. 
   He planned a little dalliance with an elven dancer he had seen performing at a Dwarven tavern. She was a free spirit and she seemed quite taken with the ruddy cheeked, bearded Dwurin (though he thought it more than possible his money had more to do with it than his looks) . Being a conscientious fellow, he was quite happy to meet her on her own terms, whatever that may be. 
   Dwurin spied a low treehouse lit by little magical lights. This was the place. As he approached he felt a strange throbbing in his head that knocked him down to his knees. The lights went out. A heartbeat or two later Dwurin saw a door in the treehouse wrench open which disgorged three tall robed figures that  jumped out onto the ground. With them was an unconscious figure that two of them carried, straddled and bound. It was the dancer.
   The robed figures moved quickly through the gloom and were seemingly unaware of his presence. In fact, they drew close enough at one stage for Dwurin to make out their faces: octopoid with tentacles writhing. He had heard tales of such creatures. Mind Flayers!
 Dwurin dutifully reported what he saw to the local elf lord, Gollendi Fairfeather. Gollendi was a little untrusting of the dwarf but such things as elvish abductions were not unknown, so after condemning the merchant for failing to stop the Mind Flayers, he and the elvish elders agreed to investigate the matter.
   Elven Witch knights utilised charmed brain moles to trace the psionic resonances left behind by the Illithids and found that they were too late. The Mind Flayers had succeeded in ferrying  the elf maid far and away to a distant world where there was no salvation.
*Near modern Mitrik in Veluna. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 14
And my mind filled with thoughts not of mineself. Of anger there be none, of frustration there be none,of compassion there be none.  Only the pounding pounding of happiness in servitude.
    The Book of Trank.  Chapter XII verse VII.
 The Mind Flayer worlds appeared untouchable. Who could resist the Illithid psionic blasts? Yet, the anger grew within the elven Eastern Oerik. Were the alien abductions going to go on forever? Could nothing be done?
   Three elvish Witch knights joined forces with two Dwarven warriors to attempt a rescue of the forlorn thralls of the Illithids. The Witch knights could harness mental powers of their own, for instance they had mastered telekinesis and telepathy. They also bathed in mystical liquids that endowed them with supernatural abilities. 
   The three rebel Witch knights were condemned by the other members of the community. The Mind Flayers were an ancient people forged in the Dragon Times. They were not to be trifled with, for their wrath could be catastrophic for Oerth.
   Nonetheless, the doughty adventurers planned to enter a Mind Flayer enclave and rescue as many abducted elves (if still alive) as they could. A brain mole was stolen to help zone in on the correct location. The Witch knights shape changed the party into Mind Flayers and infiltrated their way in.
   Mingling amongst the Illithids was not too problematic, but getting in to see the elvish abductees was a problem. Only Illithid Selectors were allowed into the slave pens, and they had to study, taste and experiment for years before they were admitted to their illustrious place within Mind Flayer society. Brain cultivation was a rarified  position that only few could hope to achieve.
   Without qualifications, our heroes couldn't hope to legitimately enter and free the slaves. The fateful decision was made to storm the area with their mighty axes and their mighty magicks. Although the Selectors were few, they were among the greatest minds in Illithid society. The psionic blasts unleashed upon the interlopers pulled flesh from bone, liquified their brains and snuffed them all from existence . 
 The Illithids discovered the charmed brain mole and used the poor animal to locate the origin of the intruders. 
   It was Oerth, and that world would pay... See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 15
"A nutritionally good diet needs  to absorb diverse sentient brains.  Breeding for different thoughts produce variety which adds to Mindfulness in the literal sense.
  For example, I have cultivated a breed of thrall that I call "block-whites.". They tend to be largish and the strain has albinism running through it.  This albinism adds a delectable tang of apricot to the flavour notes of these creatures.
  My good friend Master Thraxlbid has created a breed called "systematic brights," that tend to be of slighter build and brownish in coat.  Full of healthy insights, these creatures are delicately flavoured and add a smokiness when admixed but are a trifle astringent when devoured singularly (but dietary composition can change the quantity and quality ( See volume 2 page 476 ).
   Devouring a Block-white with a Systematic -bright blends the flavour notes beautifully, and leaves a lingering finish upon the palette.
   I have also found my thoughts sharpened and my psionics strengthened after partaking of this particular admixture."
Thought Effusions of Grand Experimenter  Gybex, Volume 2 Page 3482 See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 16
The Mind Flayers gated hordes of their thrall breeds to devastate Oerik .Block-whites and Systematic-brights, as well as other varieties of human, bred mainly for taste, were also strong and ferocious. Armed with axes and spears they fought single mindedly against the dwarves and elves, for they were in the complete thrall of their Illithid masters.
 The Mind Flayers were enraged at Oerik for daring to raid their enclave and in the  night the Illithids themselves would teleport into the dwellings of powerful leaders and kidnap them. Moradin the Soul Forger himself was ambushed, but  he wore a magic helm that thwarted  psionic attacks and he and his bodyguards beat back the Mind Flayers. 
    Moradin forged more magic helms and gave them to his elite forces this blunted many Illithid attacks. 
Corellon the Elf Lord used different tactics. They summoned  Invisible Stalkers into the Mind Flayer worlds themselves, where they unleashed their rage upon the visible realm, slaying and rampaging at will. This was an unexpected development that the Illithids had not been prepared for. They suffered unacceptable losses before they developed a mental guard that revealed invisibility. Then, in wild fury, the Mind Flayers released their reserves, the especial blend. 
These human breeds were lithe, dextrous, cunning and aggressive. With the added reserves on Oerth, the  thralls far outnumbered the Demi humans but their lack of tactics and crude fighting made them largely ineffective after their initial forays 
  Eventually, Illithids came to the conclusion that the lesser beings of the Material Plane had reached a new threshold. No longer could the sheer intellectual weight of the Mind Flayers be enough to assert full control. It was time to withdraw to select worlds of darkness and chilling rain. Let the elves and dwarves and humans destroy themselves.
   With their breeding pens stocked, and with their precious tomes and scrolls preserved, the Illithids largely retreated from the bright worlds, and those thralls on Oerik and other parts of Oerth and other Worlds (which this history covers only lightly) were released from mind control and gained their freedom for better or worse. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 17
The wars between the demi-humans and the Illithids had stretched across more than Oerik and even Oerth.  Because gates and portals were easy to conjure up 10,000 years ago, great battles and armies fought on several continents and worlds including Toril.
The outcome after the Mind Flayers abandoned the field was that a vast number of dazed, confused, humans were left behind in many places, on numerous worlds, without any 
Understanding of where they were, or why, as their minds were made blank.
 Released from bondage, they were free in theory but alien to the land, with no cultural history, no technology and, frightened, were hostile to each other and practically everything else. 
   The elves, some of whom had regretted the peace with the dwarves, saw an opportunity to grab new slaves. After all, these savages were creating anarchy in the beautiful forests and glens
   Within one hundred years very few humans  would not be in the thrall of their new keepers, the beautiful elves of the Fey. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 18
   Now we focus on the civilizations of Eastern Oerik just over 10,000 years ago. 
Most of the lands North of what is now the Nyr Dyv were wild lands.  Wood elves lived in the Vesve forest but shunned unnatural magic and were destined to become grugach elves (many sylvan elves live there today but they are from later migration).  
Some stone age humans roamed the barrens and the lands south of the Cold Marshes and up into the Burneal forest.  A few Dwarven clans lived in the Griff and Corusk mountains, although goblins, ogres, norkers, xvaarts and kobolds were more prevalent, as various noxious monsters.
Dwarves were plentiful in the Barrier Peaks, the Lortmils, the Iron hills, the Glorioles and the Hestmark Highlands.  
   Great elven nations were located in the Adri and Grandwood forests, the Rieuwood,  the Gamboge, Silverwood (which was much larger then and incorporated Hornwood, the Dim,  Oytwoid, Axewood and Dreadwood), the Bramblewood, and the Celadon. 
 All the lands including the Wild Coast, Celene, the Ulek states, the Pomarj, the Duchy of Urnst and what is now the Bright Desert were the lands of the Grey elven Celenians.  
   West of Celene were the Blemu lands, incorporating the Adri and Grandwood forests (connected as one forest then), and much of what became the Great Kingdom in the 570s CY.  The elves there were predominantly high elven. 
   The boundary between the two elven empires was loosely defined, and, in fact, many elves travelled freely over the whole of Eastern Oerik
   The elves, whether grey, high or wood, tended to be arrogant, hedonistic preeners, confident in their superiority over most other intelligent life. Dragons were a notable exception, that the elves did fear, but the great reptilian wyrms were still licking their wounds after the fall of their epoch, and were seldom seen.
   The  elven nations were linked to gates that connected Oerik with the elven empires of Kara -Tur (long gone), the elves of Kingsland and Adarus, Mystara ,and other Worlds including Toril and Krynn. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 21
   They were known as the Singing ones.  
   9000 years ago elves from Kara-Tur settled in the basin Southwest of the Hell Furnaces.  They were striking elves, perhaps the most handsome and comely of all the elves of all the world, sporting silvery eyes, skin and hair.  They had voices to match.
 Almost all of them could seen great long arias or ballads with complex harmony and profound feeling  The neolithic human tribes of the subtropical forests who heard and saw them working, feasting, gardening and playing were in complete awe.

   The WuzXi empire had suffered many indignities over these last weeks.Fires had erupted, rocks had crashed down from the sky, terrific storms had thundered and flashed. What did Tharizdun care for this? What did the Dragons think he was, some kind of creeping thing that hid in the shadows because he was too afraid to venture out into the open?
   No! Tharizdun was not afraid. Tharizdun couldn't come out into the light because Tharizdun was darkness itself!
   So, Dragons, stop with the games. Stop listening to the woodland god begging you for mercy. Come out and face the child of Tiamat, the Dragon's Breath.
          *******************************
   Corellon Larethian lay upon the bed in their guest room. Far away, his children were being tested. Could conflict break them out from Tharizdun's tendrils? Bahamut was sure this plan wouldn't work, for the WuzXi were base and wicked long before the arrival of Tharizdun, and their arrogance and rampageousness had already checked the Dragons' patience.
   Now, the decision was made. The Dragons would intervene, but Bahamut assured Corellon that they would return to rule with justice and forbearance. Oerth, as they saw it, was being destroyed in front of their eyes, and they would not sit back anymore. The Dragons had learned from their past mistakes, they said,   where ego and pride had fractured the Dragon Alliance, and the worlds had fallen into chaos. 
All will be well, Elf Lord.
   Corellon Larethian had been a child at the tail end of the Dragon Times. They remembered two overriding feelings that had haunted them when they played in the day and slept in the night. The feeling of being watched, and the feeling of being judged. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 324
   The dragons gathered together in the Celestial Palace. One of each type was there, gold, silver,, red, green, amethyst, sapphire... plus all the singular Dragon Lords, (Bahamut the Platinum dragon, the Four Season Dragons, and others) except for Tiamat the Chromatic dragon, who hated her brother, Bahamut, and still felt aggrieved at the way the Dragon Times ended, with her banished to the Nine Hells.
   Corellon Larethian was there too, an observer sitting upon a small silver chair at one end of the cavernous chamber. They had their sword and bow in easy reach despite the promise of Bahamut that no harm would come to them. The elven god relied first and foremost upon themself.
   The meeting was very long and very pedantic. The dragons argued about irrelevant details as much as the big issues. Many of the dragons refused to look at some of their cousins, or if they did, glanced upon their disliked peer with unadulterated contempt.
   Bahamut watched the fractious proceedings and was secretly pleased, because he did not look forward to the dragons ruling again.  Despite the rise of evil, good still remained.. but it was looking as if his fellow Lords would not be able to gather the dragons back together after all. There were too many enmities to overcome, after all, the Dragon Times didn't end peacefully, but was instead ugly and violent, with hatred and much vindictiveness. 
    Yet, in the end, the dragons did unite. Under a raft of conditions and caveats, temporarily and grudgingly, the majority did agree to a return of Empire, and with that, the Dragon Empire promised to deliver a sharp rebuke upon Tharizdun of Oerik.
                ************************
   Tharizdun gathered all of the WuzXi together, hundreds and hundreds of thousands, within a large valley dotted with lakes. The WuzXi had all walked there, whether near or far, and many were gaunt and almost wraith like, for they had not been permitted to stop for food and drink,  yet they all smiled broadly with dead eyes, for they were Tharizdun, and Tharizdun needed no nourishment.
   One by one, the great dragons glided down into the valley. Their scales sparkled with radiant colour, their claws and teeth white as light. Around the banks of the lakes, the dragons gathered, sitting upon their huge haunches, tails flicking and stirring up the stale air with the scent of sulphur, or cardamom, or lime, or copper...
   The WuzXi elves looked at the dragons with the eyes of the Dread God, and waited.
   The dragons spake. They were now in charge, and Tharizdun must relinquish his hold upon the Kara- Turan elves and go back to the dark cave of the Drachensgrab, where he would be permitted to lurk there to his black heart's content. The land would be restored, the forests would spring back,  the Dragons were here and their Judgement was Final.
   Through the WuzXi eyes, Tharizdun scanned across and observed each dragon in turn. They were all magnificent beasts, ancient, the greatest of their kind. If they chose, they could obliterate the WuzXi. What they could do to him was unknown. He was insubstantial, a ghost of a ghost, the accidental whelp of Tiamat. 
   The wise decision was to obey their commands, at least for now, until Tharizdun better understood his strengths and limitations, but Tharizdun was  not wise, and he hated the dragons for ordering him about as if he were a mere godling. Could a godling hold nearly a million elves in one single misty mind, as he could? Tharizdun would show his power!
   And the WuzXi elves, all million of them, made their way down into the closest lake, slipped into the water and sunk down to the bottom, smiling as they drowned. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 325
  Tharizdun plunged his vaporous tendrils into the skulls of the assembled dragons. Most resisted him, but several, the blue, the black, the green and the red, as well as the Dragon of Winter, bent their will to him.
   Tharizdun took to the air within these grand drakes, and soared over the valley, heading towards the eastern mountains. The other dragons, slow to react and still reeling from the destruction of the WuzXi, eventually realised that Tharizdun controlled the fleeing dragons, so they swept up on thermals and made chase.
   Tharizdun sent his two strongest, the Winter and the red, to turn back and battle the pursuers. The Winter Dragon, only lightly steered by the Dread God, bent their anger upon the Dragon of Spring, near the front of the  pack. 
   The orange sky fizzled and sizzled with  scarlet fire and  white blizzard, the breath attacks exploding about the dueling drakes. As the other dragons slipped through the contrails  and tried to stop the attack, the red dragon launched upon Bahamut.
   Bahamut felt his wings buckle  as the red dragon crashed into him, sending him off course spiralling torwards the mountains. Plunging after him, the red blasted fire that enveloped the Platinum dragon with yellow flame.
   With a burst of will, Bahamut tore open his wings and shot upwards, billowing out a great cloud of choking gas that stung the red dragon's eyes, blinding it as it attempted a barrel roll.
   Bahamut's elegant and tapered tail swatted the falling Red with such force that the poor controlled creature struck the mountain like a missile, sending rocks crashing down through the drifting clouds.
The battle between the Winter and Spring continued as the other dragons circled them with great wing beats. They didn't want to harm  either of them, for they were ancient relics of the Dragon Times.
   Bahamut, returned from his conflict with Red, clenched his mighty jaws together and let a part of his mind step out into the air and cross over to the Winter Dragon. He psionically connected  and his mental energies encountered the tendril of Tharizdun wound throughout the Winter's ego. Bahamut snapped out a synaptic attack that burned the metaphysical tendril, shocking Tharizdun into releasing his hold. Winter immediately rejoined their peers, roaring defiance at the Dread God.
   But Tharizdun was gone. See less

   Elehonna walked past the marching squads of orcs with open contempt. Pathetic creatures, thought the Singing One. Only their great numbers had given them their victories, yet still they struggled to conquer all.
   The silver-toned elf crossed a rude square and found herself at the entrance of the mud brick hovel Gruumsh called a palace. Half orc guards pointed their spears as she approached. Impatiently, she fished out her token that authorised her diplomatic status and the half orcs waved her in, scowling.
   Elehonna entered a bare antechamber with double doors barred at the other end. Goblin servants stood by the doors, looking bored. There was no decor to speak of, not even a rude etching. Orcs were unimaginative beasts, and the Singing One was grateful that she came from a place with high culture. She couldn't imagine how life would be without music, dance, paintings and sculptures. Oh well, she wouldn't be here long.
   After several minutes the doors were unbarred and Elehonna was ushered through.
   Unfortunately, instead of Gruumsh being behind the desk before her, it was black robed Ilneval, the ruthless orc general.
   The ugly orc looked Elehonna up and down, leering. Elehonna was well aware that she was striking, dressed in white gauze, her eyes bright and her hair silver with hints of gold. The Singing Ones were the most beautiful of all the elves, and she was proud of it.
   Where was Gruumsh? Her mistress wanted her to speak with the Emperor himself. Bring him forth.
   Ilneval pulled out a thin brush from out of a drawer and stroked it across a tusk. Gruumsh was very busy, but how could he help?
   "Lolth sent me to deal with Gruumsh directly," snapped Elehonna.
   "I understand," said Ilneval, "but why should Lolth send you, and not come herself? I mean, is an Emperor likely to speak with anyone lower than a queen?"
                  ***********************
   It was fortunate that General Ilneval was competent and not entirely lacking in intelligence. The Sheldomar district had been a continuing problem for the orcs because the halflings, gnomes and humans were always regrouping and organising resistance against the new Empire. Lolth had found them belligerent too, and resistant to reason. The Sheldomar was rich in resources and it would be of immense benefit to both parties if the region could be tamed.
   An agreement reached, Elehonna strode back out into the orcish town, and headed back to the Singing Lands, and her beloved Mistress See less

   Ulla paid the dwarf merchant then returned to her chariot. The lands west of the Crystalmists were a horse's paradise and the idea of rigging two or three horses to a small conveyance was something she hadn't seen in any other land. Apparently one of the local human tribes had developed the art, and this had given them the edge over the norkers and ogres inhabiting these grasslands.
   Two days later, Ulla reached the main settlement. Gnomes and halflings bustled about the dusty streets, passing Sheldar sitting  in the sun playing dice games. The Sheldar had not adapted very well to leaving the Sheldomar valley, but most of the demi-humans took it in their stride. There was something of the wanderer in them, and a resilience not seen in many humans. The humans thought too much.
   Ulla had nearly made it home when a falcon flew down from a roof and landed next to the chariot. With a white flash, the falcon transformed into the silver dragon, Thn're. 
   "So..." Ventured Thn're.
   "Yes, we have a deal, " said Ulla, "Three hundred more axes."
   The silver dragon stretched her muscles, her scales gleaming in the sunlight. She was impressed, Ulla was a good leader, and Thn're thought the half dwarf would get her people through these hard times.
   The Sheldomar was overrun with orcs and Singing Ones, and those halflings, humans and gnomes left were swallowed up by Gruumsh and Lolth. Thn're had long seen the grasslands behind the great mountains as a potential haven from the Orc Empire, and she had spent years laying the groundwork. She had won over the local tribes and was considered a hero in the Third Dwarven War. 
   Ulla patted Thn're on the nose. The two friends had known each other for hundreds of years, and the dragon purred. It was good that they were together again.
   "I have more good news," continued Ulla, "there is renewed fighting between the Lolth elves and the orcs. I think their alliance will soon completely fray, and then, when they all swarm about and at each other's throats, we will return to the Sheldomar and win our liberty!"
   Thn're nodded her head atop her long sinewy neck. Yes, these dark times were sure to end... See less

Part 328
1019 SD
   Sekolah tore the High Priestess apart and swallowed her with two quick gulps. 
   The sahuagin was not to his taste, her azure and pink scales were oily and her flesh was astringent, but the Shark God didn't devour her for pleasure.
   Sekolah circled his other captives chained to giant clams. His bulky but streamlined body brought terror to most of his victims, yet the sahuagin priestesses were strangely unmoved. The shark slowed and saw bubbles drift out of half open mouths. 
   "Blabidub," the priestesses burbled, "Blabidub."
   Blabidub? Sekolah knew of this terrestrial god. He had .made quite a following with the sahuagin around the island of Oeridia, but this was the Solnor sea, and his sahuagin were firmly in his power. Until now.
   The last Grand Ceremony had been a great tithing of joy for the shark. His High Priestess had delivered for him a sea elven prince along with a shipload of terrestrial elves from Ierendi. It was a delightful prize and the sahuagin must have won the day only with incredible difficulty. Sekolah remembered the beam of pride on the Priestesses face as the prince finally gave up the struggle and filled the waters with his blood.
   Then, at the dawning of a new Ceremony, Sekolah darted back and forth, excitedly  awaiting the return of the priestesses with brand new sacrifices, but they hadn't even left.
   Instead, the entire tribe of sahuagin skulked within their undersea caverns, murmuring "Blabidub."
   The bubbles floating out from the assembled sahuagin coalesced into a transparent inky sphere and rose up to the roof of Sekolah's temple, sending light ripples drifting in the waters 
   Sekolah looked at the sphere with his dull black eyes. He could feel a strong energy contained within the sphere, a sentient energy, Blabidub?
   Tharizdun looked down upon the shark eyeing him from below. Did the ugly fish not understand that the sahuagin were now the property of the Death God? He crackled with anger, but before he could launch a magical attack, Sekolah had swallowed him up!
   Tharizdun struggled inside the Great White's belly, the sphere that was his form accosted with burning acid  Tharizdun burst apart. Thousands of tiny bubbles exploded from out of Sekolah's gills, making the shark god wince with stabbing pain. The bubbles shot to the surface as Sekolah spun down and down into the depths. 
   The myriad bubbles reached the surface of the Solnor sea where they bobbed about for a moment before evaporating into a dense mist, the natural form of Dread Tharizdun.
   Tharizdun was tired of these pointless battles with powerful but insignificant creatures. He was powerful himself, but not supremely so, and that must change. 
   "Blabidub," murmured the imprisoned priestesses as Sekolah reemerged from the dark waters and glided into the underwater temple, "Blabidub " See less

   On the still of a cloudless day, Gruumsh lay in his bed, alone, and raged at the sun. 
   It had all gone wrong. Toril had all but returned to the pale elves, Mystara, led by the squat dwarves of Rockhome, was under siege, and great battles were being fought (and lost) in the central fastness of the continent.
   The Breeding Worlds were destroyed, filled with Gith spawn or Mind Flayers. No more reinforcements, untold millions of orcs dead across the material plane. Gruumsh's empire still stood, but it would not be long before his dream died.   
   Invading Oerik had been an easy task, at first. Elven nations crumbled before orcish might. Many of those early victories had been recorded in a diary. Not his, of course, for Gruumsh had no interest in scribing, but his former general, Maglubiyet, was peculiar that way. Gruumsh was sure the goblin's well recorded scrolls were kept about somewhere. Perhaps General Ilneval had them stored in his tent.
   Gruumsh returned to his dark thoughts. What happened next? Resistance had built up, the Gith had invaded, two of his best generals were defeated, the fat spider and the half-dwarf had taken the Sheldomar, and were squabbling over the prize. 
   Gruumsh had stretched out his empire too far, he acknowledged this from the heart. That had been his greatest fault. Now, he was willing to compromise, and keep his empire, after a  fashion, though it may end up being smaller than he would hope.
   Gruumsh was going to meet with his enemies, and he would negotiate terms for ending the endless war. 
   It was time for peace. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 330
   They were to meet in the central fastness of Mystara, a land of low hills, a lonely mountain, and rough woodlands. A barren field, made by the Orcish Empire after they denuded it from trees would serve as the exact point 
   Corellon Larethian represented the elves, Yondalla, the halflings, and was the voice of Moradin (who could not leave the Seven Heavens) and the dwarves. Heward represented the humans, but no one was the voice of the gnomes. Garl Glittergold thought peace talks a waste of time, and he was concentrating on thwarting the kobolds, those horned dog creatures with rat tails. The kobolds were trying to position themselves to fill the vacuum of the failing orcs and seize territory. Garl was keeping them busy.
   Corellon did not hold out much hope for peace. Gruumsh was likely attempting to delay their advance so that he could get the time needed to raise reinforcements. They would see.
   Gruumsh stood tall and proud. His black ring mail shone and in one mighty paw he held a great iron spear. He had vowed to not use it against the delegation, and he meant to keep his word. Gruumsh was truthful when he said he sought peace. Some reasonable chunks of land across Toril, Mystara and Oerik would do. Then he would stabilise his grand nations and wait a few Centuries before conquering all.
 With his keen eyesight, he saw at the edge of the horizon the advancing figures of his hated foes, and yes, they were armed too. Gruumsh hoped that they would keep their word to not strike in anger.
   A soft rain, almost like vapour, fell about the delegates gathered around a circle, their various bodyguards alert and attentive to any commands. The circle was lit by a huge flaming torch hardly affected by the rain. Sunlight hurt orcs so it was fair that the meeting was held in the dark. Gruumsh had lit the torch as a courtesy.
   Gruumsh let Corellon speak first. The ugly elf droned on and on about the terrible crimes that Gruumsh had committed, the massacres, the slavery, the destruction. So what? Such things were honourable to an orc!
   Gruumsh then spoke. He was not as articulate as the elf, but he tried to convey the beauty of his empire, how it was to be Strong and Fierce, and how the orcs would accept the lesser creatures having realms of their own, where they could rule them as weakly as they wished.
   Then the talks began to go wrong.
   Gruumsh suggested a forest for his empire, but the elf said NO! The forests were sacred and profound, holders of the Mysteries. No Orcs allowed!
   Gruumsh suggested a range of mountains and some hills. No! Said the little halfling. The mountains and hills were owned by the dwarves. Moradin would not allow it. No Orcs!
   Gruumsh mentioned some fields and meadows.
   No! Yelled the annoying human. The fields and meadows were for the Man tribes, the halflings and the gnomes! We cannot have Orcs here!
   So! These so called "good creatures" were here to trick Gruumsh! They wanted no peace! They think Gruumsh a fool! 
   With a bellow of rage, he scooped up the giant torch with one hand and raised his spear in the other.
   With his godly power, the torch burst into  yellow and red fireballs that exploded behind the delegates, setting the land from horizon to horizon aflame, and bringing forth acrid thick smoke that felled the bodyguards instantly.
   Then, he threw the iron spear into the centre of the wildfire. The spear disappeared into the smoke  but a moment later there was an enormous rumble that knocked even Corellon over. The ground splintered and cracked as if it was glass. Heward rolled towards an opening fissure but Yolanda levitated him into the air. Taking to the sky herself, followed by Corellon, the great heroes were dismayed to see the land below them shattered and broken and burning.
   "That is what I think of your land and your people!" Roared Gruumsh, "Tricksters! Traitors! The Orcs will take all!" See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 1 
Part 331
  The land was aflame for hundreds of miles in all directions. From the Broken Lands, Gruumsh raised his arm and his spear returned from the Oerth and into his outstretched hand. He gestured and with a grating crack, an enormous column of earth and rock rose up hundreds of feet, carrying Gruumsh on a wide plate of level ground. 
   Just ahead, flying above the devastation, Yolndalla and Corellon had  magically knitted together a clump of clouds upon which they laid the dazed Heward. His body sank down into the spongy texture several inches, then reached equilibrium.
   Yondalla turned to see Gruumsh watching them atop his pillar of rock. Corellon blew on the clouds and the whole billowy mass began to slowly drift over in the direction of the orc god.  
   Through blasts of black smoke and yellow and white sparks, the heroes could hear Gruumsh's harsh voice muttering up a green portal that materialised next to him. Corellon knocked an arrow and fired it at Gruumsh. It struck his neck, but despite its power and magic, it splintered into dust as it hit. Gruumsh was unharmed.
   Gruumsh had finished his spell and already something was coming from the gate ..
   It was General Bahgtru, the giant orc, unarmed save for his mighty fists. He was followed by General Ilneval, slighter but vastly more intelligent than his comrade. The two great orcs were followed by a host of half orcs and ogres. 
   Corellon fired arrow after arrow into the horde, sending many of the monsters over the pillar's edge.
   Gruumsh threw his spear and it sliced across Corellon's arm,  bringing Corellon to their knees . The spear streaked back to its master.
   Ilneval pulled out a long black hook and chain from the portal and flung it at the cloud. It hooked easily, allowing Bahgtru to pull it straight into their column.
   Yondalla rushed out, blasting blue and red energy bolts that felled some ogres.
   Heward, sword drawn, shook aside his fear and launched at Bahgtru. The giant grabbed the Flan with one paw then, as he went to throw him into the smoke and fire below, an enormous stabbing pain caused Bahgtru to drop him, which allowed Heward to roll across the stone unscathed. His Ring of Gaxx had delivered quite a shock to that stupid orc!
Yondalla was now drawing the ire of Ilneval, who was stalking her, grey sword outstretched, looking for an opening.
Gruumsh had taken another couple of arrows before he had felled Corellon, but he was unharmed. The strong shield spell he had learned after that long ago  assault on his camp that had scarred him just above his left eye, was working well. He saw Corellon still on the cloud, on their knees, bow several feet away. But the elf still had a sword in their scabbard. 
   Gruumsh strode onto the cloud, spear pointing down at the stricken elf god. Corellon drew their magnificently shining sword and danced back to their feet. The spear struck down but Corellon parried and the sword struck Gruumsh, but too little effect.
   "Ha! Little elf!" Boomed Gruumsh, "you are finished!" And the spear struck down again. See less

posts.title: A Vile Darkness
posts.text:
A History of Oerik
Book 1:
A Vile Darkness
Part 332
Ilneval felt the hot stone under his felt boots as he stalked the little halfling in her pale blue armour.
Shards of fire and sparks streaked across the platform, for the lands below the column were burning and collapsing into black rifts scarring the Oerth.
*****
Yondalla levitated above the rock pillar, trying to back away from the approaching orc. She could fly away, but if she did that her friends would remain in peril. Heward couldn't take on two great orc generals, one as strong as an elephant, and Corellon had been wounded by Gruumsh.
No, Yondalla would stay the course. She longed to help Corellon but the dangerous Illneval must be defeated first.
Illneval suddenly dashed forward and sliced at the halfling with his great sword. Yondalla conjured up a shield that took the brunt of the attack, but the force spun her about, and disoriented, she fell at the General's feet. He kicked her viciously and she grimaced.
*****
Heward had finally disposed of three half-orcs that had attempted to brain him with spiked clubs.
Dodging sparks bursting from below, nose wrinkling with the smell of sulphur, he saw Yondalla struggling to right herself as Illneval lashed at her continually. He pushed over two orcs then launched himself at Illneval who had his back turned from him.
*****
Illneval felt the full weight of Heward barrel into his back, but he barely felt it. Then the hilt of a sword crunched against his shoulder and he knew he would have to deal with the annoying human after all.
He turned about and faced Heward, whose blade was blackened with orcish blood.
*****
Yondalla shot up into the air and saw below her, Corellon desperately fending off Gruumsh, but before she could drop down and assist, a huge hand reached out and grabbed her. The hand belonged to the great arm of the gigantic Bahgtru.
*****
Bahgtru s mind was filled with thoughts.
Bahgtru got the halfling!
Gruumsh will smile!
Bahgtru will be praised!
He squeezed and felt the halfling squirm. Ha! Ha! Bahgtru wins!
*****
Yondalla felt her life force fail her. It was the end.
(No, Yondalla, My Favourite Servant. I Grant You Wrath!)
Yondalla turned white hot and Bahgtru let her go. A streak of divine fury poured out of her, engulfing the giant orc in burning radiance from the Seven Heavens.
Moradin had unleashed Yondalla's full power. She now joined the pantheon of gods!
*****
Bahgtru yelped with pain and fear.
Magic had brought him down yet again!
He staggered, them fell off the stone pillar like a falling tree.
******
Yondalla watched him tumble off the rock and crash into the boiling Broken Lands hundreds of feet below.
Yondalla now saw Heward locked in combat with General Ilneval, their swords flashing and clashing. Near them was the green lit portal, another squad of ogres coming through.
She raised her hands and a pink ray sprung from them and beamed into the gate.
The portal shuddered and distorted, then with an irresistible force, all the orcs, all the half-orcs and all the ogres were tumbled backwards and thrown back through the gate, and were gone.
******
Illneval felt the pull, but pushed back with his iron will. This proved fatal, for Heward took advantage of his distraction and impaled him through the chest.
In shock and fury, Illneval lost control and plunged into the void of the open gate.
******
The great column of rock, risen up above the flames and smoke of the rending Oerth, was free of all foes, almost...
Unaffected by the mayhem, Gruumsh was singularly focussed upon one thing: destroying Corellon Larethian.
