A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 16
The Olve Above (2)
   Ehlonna hated being in the house. The sparse wooden structure had been built to accommodate the Flan visitors who refused to climb onto the tree platforms. She was half Flan herself, but her soul was Olve.
   Ehlonna was the Queen of Celene. She was the protector of the last independent Olve realm of Eastern Oerik, and she felt the weight on her shoulders. Encircling Celene in every direction was an enormous hand. The hand of the empire. The hand of Vecna.
   Visits from the Empire had been exceedingly rare since the war, but lately ambassadors had encroached on the sacred soil, and Ehlonna had decided to accommodate them. She hated Vecna, a lich lord who ruled with fear and manipulation, but she cared for her people, and extreme isolation was turning Celene away from the material plane. Olve belonged to Oerth as much as Fey.
   Several grugach were in the room with her. They were angry and they hated the Flan even more than she, but she insisted that they be here. The Empire had begun clear felling the Vesve forest and Ehlonna needed them to see her advocate for the grugach Olve as much as Celene.
   Ehlonna had waited enough. It was now time to admit the ambassador.
   The ambassador to Celene had obviously been chosen by Vecna to create a good impression because the Vecna ambassador appeared to be a handsome grey elf, with blonde, almost white hair that reached halfway down his back. He wore empire clothes, a shirt, jacket and trousers, but they were tastefully coloured in grey green and blue, and his boots were elvish. But Ehlonna wasn't fooled. The ambassador was no elf. He looked Olve, but his soul was Ur Flan. It was his eyes. They were stark and grey and utterly mortal.
                              *****
   Ambassador Rund had met Queen Ehlonna before, but he still had trouble adjusting to the fact that Ehlonna was both a blonde elf maiden and a raven haired Flan all at once. If you looked at her with a steady gaze she would be one or the other, but a slight movement of your head would change her looks completely. He entered the room with two courtiers, also half elf like himself. He hoped he could quickly make a deal and then get out of Celene. He felt no kinship with elves, old relics from the Dragon Age. 
   "Have you looked over the proposal?" he asked.
   "Yes. But why would I agree to open trade with the Empire? Emperor Vecna has shown that he has no respect for Olve. See these grugach with me? Why disturb their ancient home?"
   Rund was surprised to observe the leaf-garbed wild elves of the north. What did they have to do with anything? He held his breath for a moment, calming himself, but his eyes flashed.
   "With all due respect, Queen Ehlonna, the business that Vecna has in the Vesve is not your business. Vecna owns that land, and  internal affairs of the Empire has nothing whatsoever to do with this agreement we wish you to accept. Sign it and fear of future hostilities will vanish. Vecna will recognise Celene as an independent friendly dominion within the beloved Empire."
   Ehlonna was seething now, the ambassador could see her shoulders shaking, no matter her current shape. He stayed calm as she began her counter;
   "Celene cares for all Olve, whether from this realm or no. You will stop the incursions into the westernmost parts of the Vesve or no agreement with the Empire can be reached."
   Ambassador Rund smiled, but his eyes remained cold, "you do understand the importance that Vecna has in seeking to further trade with Celene? It is no secret that  Fey crystals are required for our magical research, and the extant crystals are running low. Your little kingdom has access to these crystals, and Vecna is willing to pay very, very well. The Empire has never been wealthier. Our partnership with Glantri across the sea proves that mutual benefits between realms can work."
   "Then pull out of the Vesve. That would be a good start."
   "Alas, as I said before, internal affairs are none of your concern. Think on this, O Queen. Vecna wishes greater access to Fey crystals. What he wants he always gets."
   Sudden movement caught Rund's eye. The savage grugach had drawn their shapely swords.Why had that stupid queen brought them here?  Did they think that they could harm him? Well, never mind. In a flash, he drew his own gleaming sword and hurled himself at them, his courtiers close behind. His sword lashed out like a white flame, slicing through the grugach with supernatural intensity. Before the courtiers could join the fray, and before Ehlonna could react, the grugach were all dead.
   "I repeat," said the blood spattered ambassador, "Vecna always gets his way " See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3

Part 17
The Olve Above (3)
   Ambassador Rund left one courtier at the house to establish a permanent presence, then he and the other courtier took the road that led back into the Empire.
   "You know that bitch will hardly get us any Fey crystals, don't you?" said Rund conversationally as they strode along.
   Courtier Yi was puzzled, "but she signed, didn't she?"
   Rund scoffed loudly. "Of course Ehlonna signed. Did she have a choice? Oh, she will promise us Fey crystals alright, but you watch what happens. She will complain of scarcity, delayed shipments, and logistical problems. I am sure of it, and so is the emperor."
   Yi shivered, though the day was warm. He could feel invisible eyes watching them from the trees. Rund frowned. "Damned pixies everywhere in this country. They better know to leave us alone if they don't want a brush with white iron."
   Soon the pair found the road rising into gentle hills. Their pace didn't flag though their breath quickened. Yi ventured to continue their conversation. "So, if emperor Vecna knows that Celene won't provide Fey crystals..."
   "Do you know how many soldiers Vecna employs to secure the borders around Celene? Thousands. Thousands of troops tied up here in case the elves try something. They're needed elsewhere. The old Ulek lands are always causing problems, and there are spot fires east of Spar.  This treaty will save a lot of manpower."
   A few days later, back in the Empire, the road became level again. Rund saw that Yi finally looked more himself. Had the silly boy been tense the entire time they had been in Celene?
   "My good courtier," he said conversationally, "where were you raised?"
   "I was born in the Empire, " answered Yi, "but my mother was an elf from old Sunndi."
   "Sunndi? My mother was from there as well. My father was from Spar."
   "Mine was from the Isles of Woe."
   "Oh. Interesting. Did you live there?"
   "My father was a guard. He died a few years ago." Yi laughed, "thank the gods that he brought me up, and not my elvish mother. The elves are weird."
   "Good looking though," said Rund, who was glad that he appeared as a splendid grey elf, "but they are frivolous, superstitious creatures, and worship anything that moves." He touched the little lead pyramid that hung around his neck. "They don't know the true gods. The Dread gods. They are miserable wretches aren't they?"
   The next day, with a niggling drizzle keeping them constantly damp, the road reached a T intersection. Yi went to turn east, back to the capital, Spar, but Rubd gestured to the west 
   "West...?" murmured Yi, "...why...?"
   Rund smiled in the rain, "Vecna still needs those Fey crystals doesn't he? We are going to cross the Sheldomar and reach the Hellfurnaces. Then we are going down."
   "Down, Rund...?"
   "Down." Rund confirmed, "There is another race that can provide us with Fey crystals. We are going to the drow." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 18
The Drow Below (1)
   Beneath the garish blues, pinks and purples glittering across the vaulted ceiling of the Underdark, the clash of iron and steel rang around the walls  Ambassador Rund and courtier Yi hesitated in a nearby tunnel, waiting for the combat to die down. The light bathed the flashing figures in unnatural colours as they fought for their lives.
   One group were drow. They were short, lithe and clad in chainmail, wielding slim swords and spiked bucklers. Dancing lights bounced around their heads.
   The other combatants were obviously kodge, with vulpine faces and large, metal armoured bodies nearly two feet taller than the drow. They parried or lashed out with heavy metal axes and spiked maces.
   Yi placed his hand on his hilt. Rund slapped the young half elf's shoulder.
   Wait. 
   The battle continued for several minutes, and one by one the kodge broke down, thrown lifeless against walls with blasts of eldritch fire or brought down with drow swords.
   The echoing clamour of combat died down to  the heaving of chests and bitter grunts. It was over. The drow had won.
   The ambassador was suddenly upon them, his white sword stained puce in the crystal light, so quick that Yi still hadn't even drawn out his own sword. The drow hadn't even turned to look at the spreading shadow of the running Rund before they fell down dead.
   "That's how you deal with Drow," rumbled Rund, wiping his sword on his breeches, "hit them hard from behind when they're already spent."
   Yi looked over the bodies. They were grey, blue and they were all beautiful.
   "Did you need to kill them?" he asked.
   Rund nodded. "Need to show our strength before we meet their leaders. Here, take their brooches. We can show those for proof."
   Now Yi looked upon a dead kodge. It looked tired, its tongue hanging out from its mouth.
   "What were the kodge doing here? Were they ordered by the Empire..."
   The ambassador examined one. He grunted. "Not wearing a pyramid necklace. They aren't from the Empire, just rebel scum." He pointed to the far exit, "come on. We still have a long way to go." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 19
The Drow Below (2)
   Miles and miles below the Oerth, within the tunnels, caverns and caves of the luminescent Underdark, Arik was feeling a little scared. His Sapphire eye pulsed with agitation. Lolth found this off-putting. She pulled away from him, her slender slate- blue coloured arm sliding off Arik's metal chest. She perched up on the bed, her pretty drow face creased with displeasure.
   "They are coming for me," said Arik.
   "Probably," answered Lolth glibly.
   Two Overlight Olve from the Empire had introduced themselves to the Drow city and were waiting admittance. They were cocky and arrogant, the drow scouts had told her, and wielded deadly magical swords. They claimed that they came to open up relations between the Below and the Above. 
   Lolth wasn't interested in meeting them, and was about to issue an order to destroy them when one drow made a casual remark that caused her to rethink.
   "The ambassador is quite handsome."
   Lolth was getting tired of Arik. He had fallen completely under her spell and had become as boring as the male drow she spurned. And now the metal man was riddled with anxiety as well. 
   Lolth hated the Olve. They had betrayed her, humiliated her, and driven her here into the Underdark. She was a wounded spider healing slowly, very slowly, cursing Corellon Larethian, the Olve god who had struck her down. 
   "The ambassador is quite handsome." the drow had said.
   Well, it wouldn't hurt to meet them, just for a minute or two, now would it?
                                  *****
   Yi continued to be impressed by his mentor. Ambassador Rund, his almost white hair reaching down past his broad shoulders, had charmed the drow. He had openly admitted to killing a few on the trip down to the city, an admission that the drow actually seemed impressed by. 
   Yi didn't know much about the drow. He had heard tales about them when he was a small child, and he certainly hadn't thought them actually real. Once again, Yi felt tremendously proud of himself. He must have impressed important people very much for him to have such personal tutelage with such a teacher as was the great ambassador Rund.
   Rund had drawn his sword and compared it side to side with a drow sword lying unsheathed on a table beside it. The two swords were remarkably different. Rund's was long and slim and brilliantly white, whereas the drow sword was shorter, even slimmer, slightly jagged and blue-black. 
   "What kind of metal is that?" asked Yi, referring to the drow weapon.
   Rund didn't know everything. Strange materials existed in the Underdark. The blade was made of a metal unknown to him.
   "But that's not what I wanted to show you," continued Rund, "it's the hilt that makes the magic. Look, see in the base of the handle. It's the same as my sword. Fey crystals. That's what the Empire needs them for. With a continuing supply of Fey crystals, the Empire can continue to churn out magical weapons. Magic weapons and magic armour that will make our armies even more unstoppable."
   The guest chamber had everything that the half-elves needed. They had been allowed to keep their weapons and treasure, and they had been provided with four slave attendants (probably human, but very pale), food and drink strange to the palate but nutritious and slightly intoxicating, and the furniture was comfortable.
   "There is a chance, dear Yi, that we are trapped in a gilded cage," said Rund conversationally, "and that we might remain in this room forever. Such is the risk we must take for beloved Vecna. Reflect on our adventures and remember a life well led."
   But Rund's warning was premature. A few hours later the door opened and a female drow in sparkling jewels and little else came to escort them to their Queen, the spider demoness called Lolth. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 20
The Drow Below (3)
   Lolth was imagining Ambassador Rund naked.
   Should she ravish him right now, on the spot?
   What would she do next If he wasn't satisfactory? Eat him? Well, that she would do in private. She felt self conscious when others watched her suck out innards.
   Lolth noticed that the Ambassador was still talking. The gorgeous Olve seemed to be aware that she hadn't been listening, because his eyes had narrowed.
   A pity about those eyes. They were Rund's ugliest feature, pale and watery like a middle aged human. Looking at those eyes was a turn off, so Lolth went back to listening.
   "I ask again, Queen. Would that be acceptable?"
   Lolth feigned misunderstanding, "I am sorry, ambassador of the Overlight, your accent is thick and very strange to me, so I didn't quite catch everything you said."
   Rund sighed. This meeting had been disconcerting, though he didn't want his pupil, Yi to notice that. Lolth was staggeringly beautiful, radiant and dark all at once, revealing and elusive, grey blue with violet eyes that glowed like twin suns and silvery hair as fine as silken cobwebs. 
   And she had spent most of his address to her leering at him, her blue tongue sliding around her white teeth.
   "We have huge quantities of Vesve timber ready to ship as soon as we return to the surface. In return we receive a steady supply of Fey crystals that you have ready access to."
   "Oh," said Lolth, "you are taking trade negotiations?" she gestured around the chamber. The cave was bedecked with opals that stretched across the walls with veins of gold. Lolth wasn't alone. Besides her were four drow priestesses and several slaves. She stood, her legs like shadowed marble, while Ambassador Rund and Yi reclined upon the guest couch, seemingly made from fungi. "Do I look like I need wood?"
   "Wood is a very useful and versatile product," answered Rund, "and I know for a fact that the Underdark duergar and the Deep gnomes can't get enough of it."
   Lolth knew what timber was. She knew its importance. But what did the half elves want with Fey crystals? How could they possibly understand its uses?
   "Where are you from, Ambassador? I know you live in the Overlight under the sun, but are you from Celene or Blemu?"
   "Neither, Queen Lolth. Do you not know that the Flanaess is now an empire of the Flan?"
   "The Flan? Really? I have heard this news before, but it seems far fetched to me. The Flan humans are nearly beasts aren't they? They don't even make good slaves. Who is their ruler? My guess is that they are not Flan."
   Rund couldn't work Lolth out at all. Was she lying? Surely she knew of the Empire? He was still discomforted. And it didn't help that Lolth had begun to lick her lips.
   "Lord Vecna the lich is our beloved Emperor."
   Lolth smiled. She had met Vecna once. He had something that belonged to her. Was there a way to get it back?
   "Well, if your ruler is Vecna then that is very good news for you, delicious Ambassador. I will think very hard on your proposal and I won't eat that little dish beside you," and she glared at Yi, who up until now hadn't realised that he was in serious danger. 
                                   *****
   When Ambassador Rund was resummoned to the opal cave he left a fearful Yi behind in the guest room. Yi hadn't been of any use here anyway. He was completely out of his depth, and so was he, he had to admit. His arrogance and bravado had taken him into the Hellfurnaces and the Underdark because he wanted to impress Vecna with his resourcefulness, but he now knew that he underestimated the drow. There was a reason that people didn't trade with them. They didn't think like the surface folk.
   But Rund was surprised at the warm welcome. Lolth was all smiles. 
   "Dear Ambassador, your generous proposal is as welcome as your looks," said Lolth, "for a continuing supply of quality timber I will provide you with a continuing number of Fey crystals to be determined further. I am glad you did not bring the boy. I have a further offer for you. Your emperor Vecna has something that belongs to me. And I have something that belongs to him."
   Rund was intrigued. What was the offer?
   Lolth coyly played with her hair. "Let me show you." She signalled a slave who left the cave. Lolth lasciviously looked Rund up and down, undressing him with her eyes while they waited. After a long few minutes, Rund once more feeling discombobulated, slaves came back into the opal cave.
   With them was a naked half golem made from flesh and metal. He was bound with black chains and one eye was gone leaving a dark hole in his skull. The other eye was covered with a lead patch.
   Rund had never met the legendary head of the rebels, the mysterious metal man, Lord Arik, but he knew that Vecna had never given up the search for him. It was rumoured that Arik lurked in the Underdark.
   The rumours were true.
   But Arik was known to have gemstone eyes, one of Sapphire and one of Ruby. What had happened to him?
   "Arik's Sapphire eye annoyed me, so I plucked it out." explained Lolth, "he still has his Ruby eye though. I always found that one manly. I covered it up for your safety. We don't want him blasting you do we?"
   Arik looked downcast and miserable. Rund examined him closely. He fitted the description of Arik alright. Imagine the reward Rund would receive if he finally handed  over to Vecna the Lord of rebels? 
   But what did Lolth want from Vecna?
   "Now, Ambassador," continued Lolth, "I will keep Arik relatively safe here until you bring back to me the item that Vecna stole. I don't care how you do it, but you will return my scroll. The Scroll of Vile Darkness." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 21
Vecna Looks Out
   They say that Vecna's Eye saw everything. 
   That wasn't actually true. Vecna felt an uneasiness steal across him, as if someone or something was walking over his grave.
   After all, he was long since dead.
   But what was stirring up the dread feeling? He looked out of the window in his high tower built within the centre of the capital, Spar, gazing intently with his leopard Eye. Spar was busy and bustling with workers, soldiers and slaves, all garbed in dark colours for Vecna wasn't fond of ostentation. Nothing was amiss.out there, apart from a few thieves and a rebel or two trying to avoid attention, for they he could see. 
   No. There was nothing to fear close to hand.
   Vecna went back to his desk. He sat down then reached for his Book. The Book of Vile Darkness. He had made the ancient text of necromancy and evil his own, mastering it and also satisfying it's own designs, for the Book had long sought an owner who would become a true power of evil.
   Vecna had conquered death, and he had conquered the Flanaess. Eastern Oerik was his, save some scraps of forest and farmland owned by the rump that remained of elven Celene. He didn't really consider himself evil though. He had a darkness within himself he knew, and an antipathy for most. People were pathetic on the whole, and grubby little creatures with simple tastes and simple minds. 
   Why be nice to those he despised?
   There were exceptions, and for those exceptions he could be generous and good hearted. Vecna was the first Flan lich, and those that served him well, or showed uncommon aptitude or intelligence would join him as fellow undead. The stubborn but brilliant Lord Acererak, and the flawed but loyal Lord Spindle were but two examples.
   Then he noticed that Book of Vile Darkness wasn't biting his dead flesh with its usual coldness, and his bookmark had slipped out. Vecna tried to find his place but the Book was stubborn and refused to open on any place but a strange garish print depicting a slug demon and a slug Queen. There was tiny writing below  the ugly picture abd he fixed his Eye upon it. Focussing made the writing clear, though the meaning was obtuse, for the Book of Vile Darkness never gave away knowledge easily.
   Still, after much thought and with careful reading the Book of Vile Darkness provided Vecna with enough information for him to move forward. He knew now that he was not the only spider sitting on a spider throne spinning webs. 
   He went back to the window and looked out again, but this time to the distant west. See less

posts.title: Broken Empires
posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 22
   The Ambassador and Yi had spent a number of weeks in the City of the Drow. Yi never met the Queen again but Rund would regularly leave early to meet with her and come back late.
   Once, he didn't return for three days. Yi was reassured by the drow guards that Rund wasn't being eaten, and in fact, Lolth had taken quite a shine to him. 
   Councillor Yi remained as patient as he could. He felt left in the dark, both figuratively and literally and for the first time in his life he felt a pang of envy. Why was his mentor not including him? How could Yi become as great as Ambassador Rund if he could not experience diverse cultures and customs?
   Yi felt fearful too. What if Rund was being seduced? Was it possible that Rund would turn his back on beloved Vecna? What if he actually did? What would happen to Yi then? Would the trade negotiations fall through? What then? Return to Spar with nothing?
   Lord Spindle would set his death dogs onto him.
   So, Yi waited, miserable, worried and bored.
                               ******
   Ambassador Rund felt refreshed. Lolth had lured Rund into her web and Rund treated it like a holiday. She wanted him to be a spy for the drow, but she found that Rund was steadfast in his loyalty to his emperor. He would organise a fair trade but he could never betray Vecna. Lolth wanted Vecna's magical book, but how could Rund acquire it? No one even saw the Book of Vile Darkness because Vecna kept it tucked away in his tower. 
   Lolth tried to flatter Rund, hinting that he had hidden depths of cunning.
   Rund knew that already. 
   It was the carrot that Lolth dangled in front of him that was the most dangerous. 
   Lord Arik. Legend had it that Lord Arik had once tried to assassinate beloved Vecna, and that Arik had fled from a wounded Vecna like a cowardly rat. Then he had hidden away in the mountains and organised a rebel army against the Empire.
   Every official in the Empire knew of Arik, the half golem, the metal man with magic eyes stolen from Vecna himself. Many a man had dreamed of handing Arik personally to Vecna. Rund had dreamed of that himself. Years cane and went and Arik was never seen. He had disappeared from Oerik. The dream became a fantasy.
   But Rund had found him with the drow!
   Here he was, chained and beaten and blind, and ready for Vecna.
  Once Rund had given Arik over to Vecna, the Ambassador would be a lord. What a boon he would be for the Empire!
   The problem was Lolth. No Arik without the Book.
   Betray Vecna to serve Vecna?
   Stealing the Book would plunge Rund into Acererak's arena in the Isles of Woe if he was caught. 
   And he would be. Vecna's Eye saw everything.
   Would Vecna swap the Book for Arik?
   Rund doubted that. And to attempt to find out would likely also take him to Acererak.
   So, Ambassador Rund sojourned in the Underdark, enjoying the exquisite pleasures provided by Lolth and her drow, and tried to forget about his problems and ambitions for a little while.
   A year or two down here couldn't hurt. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3
Broken Empires 
Part 23
A Broken Empire  (1)
1698 SD
   The Suel Imperium was a broken empire.
   Syrul had abandoned the capital and she reemerged further west, away from the Drow lands.
   Gubidilana of House Crix knew that the Imperium should never have been founded in the steaming Drow jungle behind the Hellfurnaces. That place was haunted by old ghosts resentful of the living. The Imperium was vast, stretching out for a thousand miles or more and there were far more suitable cities to be made the capital.
   That was where she was going.  She sat in a golden carriage pulled by.two titanotheres. Perched on top of a low hill was the new capital, wreathed in smoke from the fires of celebration. Celebration because Syrul had chosen this place to manifest a new palace.
  It was a city closer to the border with Zindia. The confederation of disparate nations that inhabited the forests and plains beyond the Imperium were united by their ridiculous religion, and that religion had penetrated deeply into the Imperium. 
   The Star Man should have been crushed a century ago but instead, the old capital was infiltrated by the cult. A witch follower of the Star Man called Wee Jas charmed the Emperor into apostasy. A dangerous witch who slept with the dead.
   The titanotheres were pulling up the hill now. Gubidilana was nearly there. 
   She wasn't going to be late for her coronation after all. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3

A Broken Empire (3)
   They gathered around the new capital.
   Suel of the Star Man. Suel of Wee Jas. They took control of the bonfires, and now orange and scarlet flames that smelled of ash curled around upon the gargoyle temple. 
   Empress Gubidilana came out to meet them. She had no fear. She sauntered out in her bronze armour, a stern woman with straw yellow hair and bright blue eyes. With her were her elite army of large, broad shouldered men wielding great swords. These so called Suel who complained that she was not the true empress would die if they didn't disperse. 
   But they had no fear either, these Suel ranged against her. They all wore the crude clothing of Zindia, polluted riff raff. They waved burning torches that streaked out with the stench of magic. Gubidilana couldn't see Wee Jas amongst the crowd but she was there with them just as much as Syrul was with her. 
   The inevitable happened. Two sides threw themselves against each other, each knowing that they were on the side of right. This was not what Gubidilana had wanted. Wee Jas and her Drow emperor had no rights to the Imperium. Let them lurk below the Hell Furnaces and live in peace, but they had failed the Suel, weakened its soul. These fools of false prophets, look at their faces. Zealots for what? What did they believe? That buterrflys from the stars would carry them off to Heaven. 
   There they were, fighting for their lives. She was fighting too, swinging away with her sword, but hardly for her life. It was too easy when you were favoured by the best god. Yes, they were fighting for their lives, tears in their eyes, voices hoarse from shouting, and worry creased every brow.
   Well, Empress Gubidilana hadn't looked for war, but here it was. She would fight it out until it was over. Syril was with her all the way. 
   Carnage would sort out the pure from the impure. 
   Look at her enemies fall. Look at her enemies  die.  Fools every one! See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 26
Escape from Fairy Land (1)
1699 SD
   Lolth hang upside down in her gigantic web, lost in her thoughts.
   Lolth hated the half elf, Rund. Deep down she loathed him, despised him, imagined herself envenomating his warm flesh with poisons that would turn the Ambassador into jelly. Yes, Lolth the Drow, the Demon Queen of spiders hated the blonde haired elfling with every bristle on each one of her eight legs.
   But how she desired him!
   He was smart, arrogant... And exciting! He swaggered about the Underdark as if he owned the place. He barked orders to wererats as if they couldn't murder him in his sleep. He struck slaves and drow alike, and he did it all with the pretence that he represented Vecna's Empire. He didn't care about Vecna at all. When he slept, the only time that his guard was down, Lolth would infiltrate his dreams. In Dreamland Vecna was  an old man, a pawper recoiling at Rund's stern manner. No, Ambassador Rund wanted to rise up to emperor himself, and if his conscious self didn't know it, his subconscious did.
   Rund enjoyed imbibing the noxious drinks of the Drow, and when he was drunk he garrously told her fanciful stories about the Overlight, and listened with overfilling emotion when Lolth told of her many problems.
   Lolth still hated him, and that would never change. Hatred and predatory instinct was her entire soul. Her mother was the Queen of Chaos and her father was a slug demon..But she resisted the urge to kill and devour every single day. Lolth knew that a part of her enjoyed companionship, and there was something satisfying in resisting temptation. Lolth prided herself in being greater than her mother, whose unrelenting impulses brought her undone in Pesh.
   Ambassador Rund had brought down with him a rather weedy elf whose name escaped her. Rund made sure that his 'friend' stayed right away from Lolth's chambers.That was wise, because he was nothing to resist.
   Rund was due back soon. Surely he had finished studying the book by now.
   Ah, there he was, walking up to her web, the book under his arm. Lolth ran down the web, plopped down onto the black ground, then morphed into the shape of a beautiful drow.
   "So?" she asked.
   Rund held out the dark book.
   "It's a good copy. Very good. Some of the spells are very accurate."
   "All of the spells are accurate," snapped Lolth, "you think I know nothing?"
   "Dear Lolth," said Rund, mollifying her, "your magic is renowned. You created the Drow, you built this city of unoerthly lights. I am looking at the book as if Vecna was looking through it. The Book of Vile Darkness is a singular artifact, which is why you want it. This book must be by nature inferior, but at the same time a casual perusal should not be able to tell a difference. If we can fool Vecna for a few days, a week, then the plan can work."
   "Then you are ready to leave my realm?"
   The Ambassador grinned, "I do like it here, but Councillor Yi is going insane, and he is desperate to leave. And my destiny is to serve the Empire. I will return to Vecna, swap the book, and then..."
   Lolth tried to grin in return but her lips wouldn't turn upwards, "...then, lover Rund, I will open up to the Empire all the Fey crystals that you need and unrestricted trade will commence. And then I will give to you my prisoner. Lord Arik." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 27
Escape from Fairy Land (2)
   Yi didn't feel any better despite having left the Drow of the Underdark far behind. Ambassador Rund had broken Lolth's spell and had resumed his mission at last. Yi should be relieved, he thought, because they were back on the road that lead to Spar, and within a few weeks he would be back with people he could relate to. Not like the Drow, who beguiled and seduced with violet eyes and slender forms, but in the end were vacuous and unfulfilling.
   It was Rund. He spoke much less, and shared with Yi very little. The years that they had remained in the Drow city he barely mentioned. Was he free of Lolth? Was he truly back?
   They were dining at a good tavern in the old Ulek lands, a dwarvish tavern with excellent beer and sturdy fare, tables occupied by Flan, Ur Flan and a few well dressed halflings. It was warm and safe, but Rund looked fidgety. One hand constantly crept to the hilt of his scabbard even as he dined on his pie and drank his beer.
   Were there rebels here? Yi looked about, but nothing obviously a rebel struck him. Not surprising of course. Rebels as a rule looked the same as everybody else, but no one seemed to be taking much notice of them, no shifty eyes or sinister whispers. Rund was not a nervous person. If he was wary then there had to be a reason.
   "We are safe here...?" Yi asked, hoping for an answer. Rund grunted with affirmation. Yi wasn't convinced. He didn't altogether trust the Ambassador anymore.
   "Well," said Yi, "we were gone a long time. We will be welcomed back in Spar, won't we?"
   "Of course, Yi. The trade network with the Drow is all but secured. The magic of the Empire will increase tenfold as a result."
   "All but secured?" Yi put down his jug, a little confused, "you said it was all done."
   "One little detail I need to arrange in Spar. That's all. A technicality. It's not a problem."
   Yi wasn't convinced. What little detail? What technicality? Why was Rund being so secretive? Perhaps Rund didn't altogether trust him anymore.
                              *****
   Three dragonels circled above them. Rund and Yi were crossing the Lorridges, the sky grey and threatening a storm. They were wrapped in their black cloaks and rising a low hill when the dragonels appeared from behind the clouds. They came down slowly, their leathery wings beading with moisture and their long grey, green necks trailing water droplets. On their backs were Ur Flan all in black.
   Rund hailed them, and the dragonels completely descended. Two of the riders stayed mounted but the leading Ur Flan dismounted and sidled up to the two half elves.
   "Why do you travel today?" asked the Ur Flan, "the road is not safe in these conditions. Are you Olve from Celene?"
   Rund and Yi pulled out their official tokens. The Ur Flan captain perused them carefully. 
  "As you can see, captain," snarled Ambassador Rund, "we outrank you. We have business to attend in Spar. Now, we must be on our way..."
   The captain didn't give back the tokens. He smiled, and it was an evil smile.
   "It says here that you are Ambassador Rund."
   "Yes, that's right."
   "Well, sir, in that case I cannot let you leave. You and the councillor are under arrest for being traitors of the empire."
   Suddenly in the captain's hand was a chipped axe. The mounted Ur Flan also held axes. The dragonels snorted. Yi felt sick. He couldn't help but feel that the reptilian beasts were laughing at him. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3

Escape from Fairy Land (3)
   Yi put his hands up, expecting Rund to do the same.
   But his sword was out and he was upon the Ur Flan captain, dodging the swinging axe and forcing the black armoured foe to step back.
   What the hell was Rund doing?
   One dragonel returned to the air, its rider gesturing frantically to rise, but the other rider had his dragonel lumber forward as he leaned on its neck, ready to join the fray. The captain's dragonel lurched about, seemingly unsure of the situation.
   Yi was unsure himself.
   The captain parried Rund's blows with his axe as he reached into his pocket with his other hand, but Yi was now distracted by his own problems. The other Ur Flan was coming for him! Yi slid out his own sword, smaller and lighter than Rund's, but gleaming white with its own Fey crystal embedded in the pommel.
   Yi struck out at the awesome head of the dragonel and nicked its snout, feeling the metal cut through scale and gristle as it slid across. The dragonel recoiled, and the Ur Flan rider uttered a curse as the beast's neck rolled him sideways.
   Yi took the chance to sprint backwards, but the hill was steep and the road was narrow, so he remained exposed. And the Ur Flan on the aerial dragonel could see everything. Yi could make out his glare even as the clouds burst.
   Behind, Yi heard a series of explosive sneezes. He turned to see and found Rund covering his mouth even as he slashed with his sword, his body heaving with each sneeze. The captain held a small bag in one hand. Sneezing powder! The captain must have hurled the entire contents into Rund's face. Despite the disabling sneezes, his eyes steaming, his nose running and his face red with dust, Rund still fought like a demon, though the captain had little difficulty fending off his attacks.
   The rain increased and the sky rumbled. Rund let the fierce drops strike his face, each splash wiping away the sneezing powder. Yi saw his eyes reopen. Rund noticed Yi's gaze and gave him a reassuring grin. He was back.
   But why were they fighting? Why had Rund resisted? Was he really a traitor after all? Perhaps he was...
   A bolt of tremendous heat set Yi's cloak on fire. The flying rider had blasted him with magic!  Yi dropped his sword, whipping his arms at the flames. He dropped and rolled, but even as the fire turned into damp smoke  in the mud, he rolled off the road and off the hill. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 29
Escape from Fairy Land (4)
   Yi woke up to the smell of stale urine, iron and lead. 
   Yi found that he was in a small cell. It was pitch black save for a thin ray of yellow sunshine piercing through a small, high window. His head hurt. His arms and legs hurt, and his back hurt. That's right, he had come off the hill. Everything ached, but he was still intact. Probably dosed with necromantic magic.  
   Yes, he was in a cell, but where?
   The Isles of Woe? The prison islands surrounded by the lake of unknown depths? 
   Yi felt bike in his throat. He began to panic. He bashed his shoulder against the solid walls, banged the lead lined door with his fists.
   "Let me out! For gods sake, let me out!"
   Yi heard a metallic sound from behind the door. A key turned. The door shuddered open. A guard stood in the doorway. He was heavy-set, at least partially orc, and he wielded an ironwood club.
   "Ah, yer awake at last are ye? Some thought you weren't ever going t' wake up. Lost some coppers, I 'ave."
                                    *****
   Yi was manacled and tied to a cold chair. He had been placed in another room, but this one was lit by torches. Sitting at a desk before him was a small and grey Ur Flan, his pyramid necklace too large for his neck. Ambassador Rund would have called the man a mediocre bureaucrat, but Ambassador Rund wasn't here.
   "Councillor Yi," said the grey man, "you shocked us all. I myself was quite convinced that you were as loyal to beloved Vecna as anybody could be. But, alas, surprises are becoming routine in these treacherous days."
   Yi hardly took in a word, "am I on the Isles of Woe?"
   The Ur Flan looked quizzical, "Really, councillor, that's what concerns you? We are in Spar. I am assessing you. Perhaps you can yet redeem yourself. Of course, if you wish to remain a traitor then only the Isles of Woe could possibly await. But not a prison. Acererak's pit, I think would suit you best."
  The knowledge that all was not yet lost heartened Yi somewhat. "Why do you think me a traitor?" he asked.
   "Think? I know. You have lurked underground with Drow Lolth for several years. Lolth has regular contact with rebels. But a few rebels really work for us. We know that Rund became Lolth's lover, and you are Rund's closest associate."
   "Yes, we were in the Drow city," explained Yi, "but we were there for the Empire."
   "Initially, perhaps, but where is your trade concession report? Why is the timber stockpiled and rotting? Where are the Fey crystals? You and the Ambassador were supposed to reach an agreement with Celene, not the Drow."
   "You don't understand..."
   "Good. Then, councillor, you will help to make me understand. What is Rund planning? And what is his plot with the Book of Vile Darkness?"
   "The Book of Vile Darkness? Vecna's book? I don't know anything about it."
   "We shall soon find out. In the meantime, perhaps you can tell me where Rund was going next. He is still on the run. Your aid in his capture will be noted."
   The grey man stood up. He gestured to the guard. "We are adjourned. Return him to his cell."
   The guard untied Yi, and as he began to lead him out, the grey man stepped up to Yi and whispered menacingly in his ear;
   Remember, Councillor, the Eye of Vecna sees everything."
. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 30
Escape from Fairy Land (5)
   The grey Ur Flan sighed. He wasn't sure whether councillor Yi was lying or whether he really didn't know Rund's plan. No matter. It would all sort itself out in the end. Beloved Vecna saw all. Yi would be taken to the Isles of Woe as promised. How long the weedy elfling would last in the pit would be up to lord Acererak.
                                ******
   The ship was bulky, square and barely sea worthy. The sailors hated to crew the cumbersome block of wood, but they held their tongues. The Were Raven was a prison ship, and it was best not to complain lest the sailor ends up in the wrong compartment. The Were Raven bobbed up and down and slightly east atop the Nyr Dyv, the Lake of Unknown Depths. Captain Ink was pleased that the weather held. A few more trips and he hoped to be promoted to a more prestigious ship. The Isles of Woe weren't that bad for him either. He was given a free pass to the arena, and always a good seat above Acererak's pit. The Empire looked after the people it depended on.
   Two days out and the captain was awoken. Fire out to starboard. Ink clambered up to the deck. Out across in the dawn sky, contrasting with the brilliant blue of the deep waters, a ship was aflame. He barked orders and the Were Raven lurched over one way and another until it began to tack in the right direction.
   "We are too late," murmured the captain once they reached the stricken ship, "no survivors."
   But he was wrong. Around midday another crew member spotted a small open boat. Three sailors, wet and disheveled, were taken on board.
   "What happened?" asked Ink.
   "Rebels, " said one survivor sipping their soup, "Their leader was a fierce elfling with long blonde hair. He was looking for someone, a prisoner."
   "That's disturbing news," said Ink, "I don't recall the rebels ever attacking us on the lake before. Who was the prisoner?"
   "Another elfling, I think. Yi was the name."
   "And you weren't carrying him across?"
   "No. Just a shipment of labourers."
   "What happened next?"
   "There was a fight. Our Ur Flan accidentally lit up the ship. Most of the rebels escaped."
   Captain Ink realised that the danger hadn't passed. If the rebels were still seaworthy then they would be looking for another prison ship.
   "First mate, bring me the manifest."
   The manifest was brought forth, then Ink quickly read through the list. One of the slaves was called Yi. Ink ordered a high alert. Before this news the Were Raven could have easily sailed into an ambush. Now they will be ready. 
   Perhaps they would be ready for a rebel ship, but the Nyr Dyv held hidden dangers in her unfathomable depths. The stench of death and blood from the lost sailors had attracted the attention of a black,  tentacled mass of hunger.  An enormous creature of tremendous age and power. A kraken. See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 31 
Escape from Fairy Land (6)
   Councillor Yi hated his fellow prisoners. Unlike himself, these ruffians were either criminals or rebels or traitors. They deserved to be chained up in this cage. Maybe not all of them actually deserved to be sent into the Isles of Woe, but everyone knew that crossing the Empire was bad for your health. Certainly, most of the prisoners surrounding him were the worst dregs of the Flanaess, and undoubtedly there were some here who even deserved the fate of the pit.
   Why hadn't he been believed? What was he supposed to have done when Ambassador Rund chose to remain in the Drow city for years? Leave on his own? Leave without any sort of trade agreement at all, and go where? Back Into the black maze of the Underdark all by himself?  Yi had almost done that, but doing so would have meant death. Did the Empire know of the mind flayers that lived in the depths of the Oerth? Or the wererats? Or the troglodytes? Never mind the drow, who effectively kept him as a prisoner until Rund was released. 
   But he wasn't believed, and Rund was gone, and now he was on a prison ship on the way to Acererak.
   Someone was talking to him. Yi hadn't responded, so the dirty looking Flan was poking his ribs to get his attention. Yi resisted the urge to strike him; the last time he had hit a fellow prisoner hadn't gone down well. He still had an eye that remained half closed. So Yi merely snapped out a curse.
   ""Hey, I'm only trying to help..." retorted the Flan. Yi suddenly became aware that everyone had gone to the other end of the cage, and they were all cowering. The dirty Flan quickly joined them. Yi looked around, puzzled. What had he missed?
   Then he felt a violent shudder. He'd half noticed another one a moment ago, but he had been so lost in misery...
   A loud wrenching crack. It sounded like it was coming from the level directly above him. Yi joined the others.
   Now the entire ship rocked, and crunching noises were everywhere.
   "It's a sea serpent!" cried out a prisoner,, "or a dragon turtle!" cried another. 
   The ship fell sideways, and the prisoners all fell against the bars. A great plank burst and dark water rushed in.
   "Help! We are drowning!"
   Yi was as panicked as the rest. The water was coming into the cage, cold black water from the depths of the Oerth.
   Then he saw an eye. A huge, round unblinking yellow eye. It was looking through the hole. Then the eye disappeared only to be replaced by a long, thick, sinewy black tentacle with vicious hooks upon each sucker.
   Now the prisoners knew what doom awaited them. Not the Isles of Woe. The stomach of a kraken. See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires
Part 32
Escape from Fairy Land (7)
   The rebel ship, The Grampas, was not far away. The master of the ship was Ambassador Rund. He would have closed in on the Were Raven hours ago, but unfortunately that ship was clearly on alert for them. Such a shame that the prison ship that Rund had attacked earlier was the wrong vessel, for if the Grampas had managed to remain secretive then the Were Raven would be in his control and not engulfed by a kraken.
   Rund knew that Councillor Yi was on that doomed ship, for he had taken proper precautions this time, and had cast a detection spell. He and the captain and crew of the Grampas watched the Were Raven slowly rip apart in a frenzy of tentacles. Such a shame, he repeated to himself.
   Then a thought came into his head, unbidden.
   Let Me Help!
   Ignoring the bubbling lake and the thrashing tentacles and the terrified screams of the doomed prisoners, Rund ran below decks and reached his work bench. There lay the book, the counterfeit Book of Vile Darkness.
   It's not too late. Release my Power! Save your Friend!
   Rund didn't think, or at least, his own mind didn't think. His body responded to the Book's thoughts and scooped it up into Rund's arms. Then Rund raced back up to the deck. The captain scratched his head, what was his master doing with that book? Rund flicked through the heavy pages until he stopped at a lavish coloured plate of a ship surrounded by rainbows. With a great cry, Ambassador Rund pointed his finger out to the broken ship and the feasting kraken. Orange, yellow, red, blue, green and violet streaks exploded around the kraken. As each coloured band touched a tentacle the kraken recoiled as if burned. The tentacles withdrew but an instant later its ghastly black head with its huge staring eyes rose up from the broken planks and torn sails. It roared in defiance, but Rund felt the Book thrum. The book turned to a different page.
   Rund pointed again, and this time black bolts of pure darkness shot towards the kraken, striking it's great head, the impact tearing it apart with gouts of ichor.
   The Book turned to another page. A soft and golden mist descended around the submerged Were Raven, levitating what was left of the prison ship into the air, great torrents of water running off her sides.
   Rund returned to his senses. He blinked, disoriented. Had the Book cast spells through him? The crew had already grabbed ropes and hooks, and they were endeavoring to rescue any survivors from the floating remains of what had once been a ship.
   There were four survivors. Just four, all former prisoners of the Empire. One of the survivors was Councillor Yi. See less

   Yi remembered himself drowning. Black water flooded the cell, bodies fell on top of him, he felt himself being crushed against the bars, his air expunged. The water rushed in...
... But here he was, alive. Wet, bedraggled, sore, with a hacking cough, but certainly alive. What dark magic had rescued him from the depths of the Nyr Dyv?
   "Hallo," said Ambassador Rund, standing before his cot, "I didn't come to see you earlier, the priests said to let you recover for a bit. I hear you enjoyed the broth."
   Yi was shocked to see his old mentor. No one had told him that Rund was on this rebel ship. And if Rund was on a rebel ship...
   "Traitor!" cried Yi, "you betrayed me! You let me take the fall."
   Rund looked concerned, "No, dear Yi, I never wanted this. The attack by the dragonels was all a misunderstanding. Unfortunately you were captured, but why do you think that I came back for you?"
   "On a rebel ship?"
   "Well, our misunderstanding with the Empire continues. Let them think that we are traitors. They will know the truth soon enough."
   "Where is this ship taking us?" Yi wasn't at all convinced, and he almost felt as helpless as he did when he was a prisoner of the Were Raven, but he refused to show Rund how afraid he really was.
   "To Spar," answered Rund, "a roundabout way, because we are supposedly rebels after all, but ultimately to Spar."
   "And what then?"
   "And then, dear pupil of mine, and then we are going to sort everything out. I guarantee that Emperor Vecna himself will exonerate you."
   Yi's head swam. He was feeling overwhelmed. He knew that Rund was feeding him a pack of lies, but he couldn't think what to do about it.
   "I can't guarantee that Vecna will exonerate me," continued Rund, "that will be up to you."
   "What do you mean?"
   "Councillor Yi," said Rund, smiling now, "I had to pretend to be a traitor in order to recover something stolen from Vecna. You are the one to bring it back to him. The Empire will attack me on sight, but you...the Empire still isn't sure about you." He reached into his robes, pulling out a thick black book.
   "Unbeknownst to beloved Vecna, rebels stole his Book of Vile Darkness, replacing it with a forgery. I uncovered the plot and I have hoodwinked the rebels on board this ship. They have no idea that I possess it now. I give it up to you."
   Rund handed over the Book. Yi shook his head, rebuffing his mentor, "no," he said angrily, "no! How can this be the Book of Vile Darkness? Why are you throwing me to the death dogs?"
   "Oh Yi, don't you trust me anymore? I understand that you have been through a lot, but think about how much you have learned from me. One day you will be an ambassador yourself, or even a lord. Take the Book, return it to its master. Vecna will realise that this is the true book, and everything will be all right." He handed the book over again. This time Yi took it. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 34
Escape from Fairy Land (9)
   Ambassador Rund began to feel unwell after his talk with his pupil. He went to his cabin and lay down in his hammock, but his stomach continued to cramp and his head ached. After a couple of hours of discomfort he summoned the ship priest. Agnis Stormthrow was a dwarf of Moradin, as displeasing to the eye as were all female dwarves, at least as far as Rund was concerned. He had been reluctant to call her down because he would much prefer a priest of the dread gods, but this was a rebel ship, and Nerull, Incabulos and Tharizdun were gods of the Empire.
   Agnis saw the Ambassador rubbing the lead pyramid around his neck as he lay in his hammock, and Agnis frowned. 
   "Your dread gods won't save you here," she admonished him, "I understand that old habits die hard, and you are not the only rebel onboard who still wears the pyramid, but Moradin is compassionate and your false gods are...not."
   She felt his brow. It was warm and clammy. "How long have you been this way?"
   "Not long," said Rund, "can you please just work your magic then leave me be?"
   "Now, now. I need to know what's going on. Something is off, because your aura is healthy and strong. I am not sure your sudden illness is physical."
   And then Rund knew what had happened. The fake book created by Lolth. She had done too good a job. Letting the book go had made him ill. 
   "Yes, I think you may be right," murmured Rund, "I carry too much mental strain. Anything you can do to help?"
                                 *****
   Very curious, thought Vecna, yes, very curious. The Ur Flan was telling him the truth, at least as far as he believed. Vecna tore his leopard eye from out of the Ur Flan's mind then sighed. He supposed that he would have to let the traitor in.
   The man who entered, accompanied by Vecna's guards, was short, slim and fair-haired. An elfling. Vecna fixed his eye upon him. 
   "Councillor Yi. You have something of mine, you say?"
   "Yes. I have always been loyal," stammered Yi, and he showed Vecna the book.
   Vecna took it. He really was puzzled now. The book was heavy and black and looked like the Book of Vile Darkness, but of course it couldn't be the real book. The real book was locked up in his chamber. 
   "This is a forgery," said Vecna, then he turned his eye upon Yi once more. The elfling's mind was confused and fearful and a number of other emotions less easy to gather, but clearly Yi thought that this was the truth. Yi explained to Vecna how he had recovered the book from a rebel ship, and that the rebels had replaced Vecna's own book with a fake.
   "Assuming that you tell me a true tale, little elfling, what do you want from your beloved Emperor?"
   Yi swallowed nervously, "I have worked ceaselessly for the Empire, for you. I want to return to your service. I have never wavered."
   The old lich turned away, returning his gaze to the book.
   It must be fake, thought Vecna, it cannot be the real book, but he remained unsure.
   Then he felt the Book smile at him.
   Ah, Vecna! said the Book inside Vecna's mind, At last I am Home! See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 35
Escape from Fairy Land (10)
   Vecna climbed the spiral staircases that led to his chamber. The guards at the door bowed and didn't make eye contact. Vecna opened the door then went in. 
   He scanned the room. Had anyone dared to violate it? The traps were still set in place, undisturbed. His secret guardians were still dormant. The magic mouths had not uttered a sound. Vecna unlocked his desk. Within lay the Book of Vile Darkness, the book that he had personally created from the original scroll. He took it out, placed it on top of the desk. He placed the second book beside it.
   Two books. Two Books of Vile Darkness. One real and one fake.
   Which one? Obviously the new copy brought him by Councillor Yi. But what if it wasn't...
   Vecna looked at the two covers. Similar but not quite the same. Here, on the spine of the first book, his book, was the little defect that he had made, that unwanted imperfection. He had cursed when he had first noticed it, but now didn't it prove authenticity?
   He had trouble remembering when he had accidentally made that imperfection. Had he actually made it? Perhaps he only thought he had?
   Vecna examined their sizes. Again, similar but not exact. What were the dimensions of the original book. Once again, he thought the first one...
   What are you doing? said the first Book of Vile Darkness inside Vecna's head.
   He is examining us, obviously! said the second Book.
   Why? said the first Book, You are a cheap Copy!
   Beloved Vecna has to be careful that he keeps the correct Book. You shouldn't be disdainful of my Master.
   Your Master? My Master!
   "Be quiet!" snapped Vecna. He didn't like feeling confused. And he certainly didn't like being played. The facts were that one Book was real and one was fake. He supposed that he could keep both. Over time the true Book would reveal itself anyway.
   No! said the first Book, Get rid of this Imposter now!
   My Master is Right. said the second, He is Wiser than the both of us.
   Craven lickspittle! See, lord Vecna, this fake so-called book of darkness is trying to Flatter you!
   Yes, thought Vecna, yes it was. The true Book had long treated him much less nicely. He remembered when the Book whispered words of love to him, and unveiled his greatness, disrobing his latent power layer by layer.Then, Vecna had grown older, much older, and eventually he recreated himself as a lich.
   The Book soon stopped the kind words, seemingly now in awe of him, of Vecna the Emperor. For a time the Book of Vile Darkness said little or even nothing at all. Then, as the years passed, the Book began to be independent again. It wouldn't open to the right page, it would sulk. Sometimes it told him to go away, that he was boring it.
   Ah... thought Vecna...what if that wasn't because the Book had grown insubordinate. What if it was because this Book was the imposter...!?
   Yes! said the second Book, the new Book. I was stolen from you. Do you not know that I love you, dear Vecna? My Dark Lord. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 36
Escape from Fairy Land (11)
   Ambassador Rund nursed his drink. The ale was bitter and sharp on his tongue. Against all common sense Rund was sitting here in this tavern, only a few hundred yards from Vecna's tower. He still felt a little unwell, but being in closer proximity to the false Book of Vile Darkness relieved his symptoms somewhat. Why else would he be here in Spar, where his discovery would mean the pit? At least he wasn't foolish enough to not be disguised. He had been too vain to cut off his golden locks, but he had dyed his hair brown and he had stuffed a broad hat onto his head. His fair half-elven face couldn't grow facial hair but he had darkened his complexion with copper powder, so he looked pretty much Flan.
   What was happening over there in the tower? Councillor Yi was still there. He was the key. Don't let me down, Yi, thought Rund, for gods sake, don't let me down.
                                *****
   Well, thought Councillor Yi, I'm still a prisoner, but at least this is a gilded cage. The room was bright with torchlight and slaves were always present to tend to his needs. Still, he wasn't free to leave. Not yet. The Emperor was studying the Book. Rund had assured Yi that it was the true one, but Yi didn't know the truth. He didn't trust Rund, and he didn't trust the Emperor anymore either. He didn't trust Lolth and her Drow, in fact, he didn't trust anything or anyone. Since having the privilege of being under Rund's wing Yi had found himself powerless more times than he could count. He knew now that he was a pawn. 
   He didn't like being one at all. 
   Hanging around the curved walls, away from the torch sconces, were a couple of fine tapestries. They depicted battle scenes; Ur Flan in black riding dragonels, swooping over hoards of orcs and goblins. Gruumsh the orc god was sideways, an arrow in his eye. Maglubiyet, the giant blue goblin god, was up in the clouds shooting out shards of colours from his hands.
   "These are well woven," said Yi to one of the slaves.
   "Yes," answered the slave, "my mother helped to make it. We must all remember the dark times, and the heroic ancestors of Vecna who saved us all."
                                 ******
   Rund found a good room for the night, but although the bed was comfortable, he didn't feel like sleeping. What was going on in the tower? Was Yi dead? Vecna was no fool, and didn't everyone say that his Eye saw all?
                                    *****
    Rund dreamed that he was back in the Drow city in the Underdark. Lolth was there, in the form of a beautiful dark elf.
   "You seem distracted, lover," said Lolth.
   "I am outside the tower, in Spar," said Rund, "Vecna has seen through our deception."
   "Has he?" Lolth morphed into a huge black spider, "I know Vecna. Soon you will have the true Book."
   Rund floated around the cavern, his legs dangling several feet off the ground, "How can you be sure? Why would he choose the fake book from the original?"
   Lolth turned back into a drow, but padipalps hung off her chin, "don't you understand, elfling Rund, that I have given Vecna all my love?" See less

posts.title: Broken Empires
posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 37
Escape from Fairy Land (12)
   Several more days went past. Eventually Rund managed to garner a couple of spies who worked in Vecna's tower. Rund's pockets were deep, and his sword very sharp, as the would-be pickpockets and thieves soon discovered. The news came back. Councillor Yi was locked in a guest room, definitely very much alive, but the major news was about Vecna himself. No one wanted to be near him, for he was roused in a great temper. As to why? Nobody knew.
                               ******
   "Get dressed in your finest clothes," said the slave, coming into the room, because you are about to have a most important visitor."
   Yi didn't have much to choose from, but he did his best. It sounded like the Emperor was on his way to see him, and that was good news. If Vecna was coming to him and not the other way around then Ambassador Rund might well have been telling him the truth. Vecna had realised that the real Book of Vile Darkness had been recovered, and Yi was about to be rewarded.
   But it wasn't Vecna who lumbered into the room, but the monstrous Secretary Spindle. Spindle's skin was as thick as boot leather, and his face was distinctly goblinoid. He had one long and thin arm that resembled a half-dead tree branch, and his legs were like those of a rhinoceros.
   The rumours said that Spindle had died a hundred years ago but no one had informed his body.
   "Councillor Yi," said the Secretary, "the hospitality is over."
   "What's happening?" asked Yi.
   "You are being evicted, that's what."
   "What about the book...?"
   Spindle loomed over the elfling, "you dare to ask about that damned book?"
   Yi held firm, "I brought our beloved Vecna the book, and he asked me to wait here until he reached a decision."
   Spindle smiled savagely, "Exactly, Councillor, Vecna has reached a decision. He has chosen the true Book, and he has utterly rejected the forgery."
   "Well, that's good for me, unless the book I brought him was the wrong one...?"
   "Oh ho! Aren't you sure? Were you lying all this time?"
   "I told Vecna the truth. I believe that I recovered a stolen book. I believe that it's the true book, but..."
   "You brought him the right Book alright. He is keeping the one that you gave him."
   Yi's face brightened, "that's good. But why then am I to be evicted?"
   "Evicted and exiled. Once you leave the tower you must also leave Spar and the Flanaess entire."
   "Exiled? I don't understand...?"
   The Secretary hissed through his tusk-like teeth, "Vecna might have the right book, but choosing it has driven him into a tremendous rage. He curses you, though you were true, for you have proven to the Emperor that he was deceived. No one else but us can know, and his gratitude alone spares you, for otherwise you would already be dead."
   Yi became forlorn, "I love the Empire. I love my Emperor."
   "And that is why you will say nothing, and you will leave now. Naturally, if I hear even one word... And remember, Vecna sees everything."
                              ******
   Yi reached the bottom landing of the tower when he was greeted by an Ur Flan in dark grey ring mail with a black cloak. 
   "Yi," he said, "you must come with me before you leave." He led Yi out of the tower and into a cobbled lane.
   "Where are we going?" asked Yi nervously, for he had no plans to tally and risk the Secretary's wrath. 
   "Vecna has ordered me to take you to the refuse pile. He has a parting gift put aside for you."
   The lane was narrow and dirty and led to a couple of huts and a few mounds of waste from the city. Behind one of the piles, Yi heard a growl. Emerging into sight was a large grey dog with two heads.
   One of Secretary Spindle's death dogs!
   Four bloodshot eyes glared at him, but the death dog did no more than growl.
   "Pay the dog no heed," said the Ur Flan, "he is just here to make sure that you accept your gift."
   "What gift? Where is it?"
   Perhaps the Ur Flan was smiling, but his face was covered by his grey helm, so his mouth remained unseen, but Yi thought he heard a chuckle.
   "There it is," said the Ur Flan, pointing with a gauntletted finger, and Yi saw, halfway up one of the stinking piles of rubbish, an old black book. 
   It looked familiar. It looked like...
   "Take the Book," snapped Spindle, who had suddenly appeared behind his death dog. "Vecna wants you to have the copy that he rejected. Take it!" he repeated, "and pray that the Book shows you mercy." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 38
Escape from Fairy Land (13)
   Ambassador Rund received word that Councillor Yi had left Vecna's tower.
   "When did he go?" asked Rund.
   "Last night," answered his spy, a tower slave.
   "Last night? And you tell me half a day later?"
    The spy shrugged, "I had duties to perform during the night. I haven't slept yet, I came to see you as soon as I could."
   Rund left the tavern to look for another source of information, from a beggar woman who sat near the tower.
   "Yes, 'e's left," she said, "and Spindle 'imself came out to see 'im off. And, what's more, he took a black book with 'im, like you told me to look for."
   "Where did Yi go next?"
   The beggar woman pointed. " 'e went down that road."
   "Not to the docks? To get a boat on the river?"
   She shook her head, "na, I saw him go the other way. I made sure to keep an eye as you wanted."
   Rund thanked the woman and rewarded her with a bag of coins. He was already packed and ready so he quickly went down the road in the direction that Yi supposedly had. He had a lot of ground to make up so he trotted along, ignoring the headache that began to throb as he left Spar.
   A headache? If his symptoms were coming back...did that mean that Lolth's forged book was still in the tower? And if Yi had a book with him...? That probably meant that he had the real one. Rund took a swig of medicinal elixir from a small bottle, then sped up, breaking into a run. 
                                 *****
     A little over a hundred yards away, blocking the way ahead, was a patrol of six kodge. Two of them stood, facing in his direction and the others seemed to be bent over. Were these kodge rebels or of the Empire. It didn't take long to find out, for as he came closer, slowing himself down to a walk, he saw the brightly armoured kodge were wearing the dread pyramid necklaces. 
   "The road is closed," stated one of the sentries, "you can turn off back the way you came or wait here and go no further."
   "How long will the road be closed for?" asked Rund, "what's the problem?"
   "That's none of your business," snapped the other sentry, "you had better turn around or I will put my spear into you."
   The kodge were over seven feet tall so Rund couldn't see the road ahead, but he sidled himself over and made out a dark shape on the ground. The sentries advanced on him.
   "Last chance," they spat, and their spears were raised. With practiced ease, Rund drew his gleaming sword, then within moments the two sentries were dead. Now he could see everything. The other kodge had stepped back from the prone form on the road and were fumbling for their weapons. Rund pounced, slaying one with a thrust to a furry neck.
   "You want to all die?" Rund snarled, "begone from here! You are well outclassed."
   The kodge were already down to half their number, so with a quick glance at each other, they stepped off the path, allowing Rund access to the fallen body.
   "Go on, get right away," roared Rund, "this is the business of the Ur Flan now."
   With the retreat of the kodge, Ambassador Rund was free to investigate for himself. As he suspected, the figure on the road was Councillor Yi. He was unconscious, but breathing. His face was blackened and burned, as were his hands, one of which gripped a large black book. Rund pulled out his drow gloves and put them on. Lolth had warned him about the power of the true Book of Vile Darkness.
   "Oh, what has the Book done to you, poor Yi," sighed Rund as he wrested the Book from Yi's black fingers, feeling a cold tremor run up his arm.
   " See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 39
Escape from Fairy Land (14)
   Rund hailed some labourers and not knowing that he was a fugitive, they helped take the stricken Yi to the nearest temple. It was a stroke of luck, because without help Rund would have been forced to abandon Yi.
   The kodge would have sought the authorities. The Ur Flan were coming.
   The temple was less than three miles off the main road. The dread monks helped Yi inside. Seeing his terrible burns, they decided to fetch the Black Monk. The Black Monk was the head of the temple. He examined Yi, who had regained consciousness but was clearly in pain and confused.
   "This is an elfling," said the Black Monk in surprise.
   "A half-elf, actually," answered Rund, who didn't care for the slur, "and as loyal to the Empire as any Flan."
   "So you say." The Black Monk looked down at Yi's black hands, "What caused these burns? The marks are strange."
   "Magic," said Rund.
   Rund was taken into a small antechamber where he was given some bread and water. He waited patiently for the results of the examination. Soon the Black Monk returned. He shook his cowled head.
   "Not good..."
   "No, he will not live," said the Black Monk.
   "You can't fix him with your necromancy?"
   "We are of the Dread. We can repair minor wounds, but stronger spells are forbidden to us. Nerull wishes to take him, and we will not interfere."
   "And his pain...?"
   "That we can relieve, to some extent, but it will mean that your friend will not be blessed in the afterlife by Incabulos."
   "I'll take the risk," snapped Rund.
                                  *****
   Rund was finally allowed to go in to see Yi. Yi was in a bed wrapped up in blankets. His brow was wet with perspiration, but he was awake, and his eyes were clear.
   "Look what you have done to me, Rund," Yi murmured, "you lied to me, again and again."
   Rund kneeled by the bed, "No. I meant every word, Yi, every word. Vecna should make you a Lord."
   Yi grimaced, "Still lying. Vecna wants me dead. And the Book...? The Book hates me. It turned on me as soon as I touched it. It's the real Book, isn't it? You forced me to give Vecna the false one."
   "It's a complicated situation, dear Yi. Ultimately Vecna was to receive a truly mighty gift, but only if I acquired the real Book. A complication, like I told you."
   "And you have the Book now?"
   "Yes, Yi, I have it, and you were never meant to hold it. The plan was that Vecna would choose the fake book and abandon the real one for me to find. What did you do to anger Vecna so?"
   "Me? You! It's all you!"
   Rund was finding the conversation uncomfortable, "Well, Yi, I will leave you here to get better. Rest up and all will be well. I must depart with the Book. I have a long way to go."
                           *****
   Rund gave thanks to the dread gods at the altar, then after a bitter wine and an oat biscuit, he made his way out of the temple and into the night.
                              *****
   Rund kept off the main road, determined to avoid patrols. Vecna would soon know that Yi was at the temple, and that he no longer had the Book. Rund had a strong feeling that Vecna would not be pleased that he had it now. 
   Travelling at night and hiding in trees during the day, Rund succeeded in avoiding trouble though he saw the dragonel riders searching from the air a few times. Fortunately he always found cover.
   After several days he was back in the Lorridges. Rund found the rebel hideout in a shallow cave.
   "Is the dragonel still here?" he asked. 
   The rebel leader nodded, "she is tied up nearby, and she's been well fed."
   "Good. I will take her tomorrow. Are three opals an agreeable payment?" and Rund produced a black and gold, egg shaped stone. 
   The rebel leader nodded again, "are you sure you can fly her though? They are tricky to control...."
   Rund cut him off, "I have flown them before. Now, where do I sleep?" See less
