A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 40 
Escape from Fairy Land (15)
   Ambassador Rund flew west. He flew the dragonel high, and the pterosaur-winged beast seemed to enjoy the sensation of rushing air. After all, Rund thought, the dumb beast had been tied up ever since the battle Rund and Yi had with the Ur Flan. The aerial patrols ignored him. Rebels didn't take to the sky.
   Rund camped in high, out of the way places, far away from any roads. There he could light a fire and roast whatever game was roundabout. On the third evening as He plucked a fat brown bird,  he considered his fortunate situation. Rund was extremely pleased that the plan had worked, at least after a fashion, and that the book of Vile Darkness was now in his possession. He kept the Book in a bag. His gloves had protected him from poor Yi's fate, but his arm even three days later was still tingling with cold. Even concealed within the bag, Rund could feel the Book radiating pure hatred towards him.
   Well, soon the Book would be Lolth's problem.
                            *****
   It was good to be back in the Underdark, thought Rund, as he strode down the wide tunnels triumphantly. 'Fairy Land,' Yi had called it, though for Yi the dazzling crystal caves were a prison. Rund had dropped his disguise of course, and his hair was brushed up into a blonde mane.  Drow recognised him at once and the blue grey elves escorted the proud half-elf to their Queen.
   Lolth greeted him warmly, her beauty casting dazzling shadows. She knew he had brought the Book, for drow had raced ahead to inform her.
   "Are you sure this is Vecna's Book?" she asked.
   "See for yourself, " said Ambassador Rund, and placed the bag at her feet.
   Lolth opened the bag and took the Book. Rund saw her face grimace in pain, but she soon mastered it, her violet eyes flashing anger, and she struck the cover with her other hand. Then, Lolth turned about, ordering all of her drow out.
   "You too, Ambassador Rund. Go into our quarters like you used to do. I need to be alone with my Book." See less

posts.title: Broken Empires
posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 41
Escape from Fairy Land (16)
   Lolth wasn't completely alone in her cave. Almost entirely forgotten in a shallow alcove was  the half metal and half man golem called Arik. Arik was still bound in chains, still without his Sapphire eye and his Ruby eye was still sealed over. Blind, miserable, impotent, but still aware, Arik seethed, plotting dark revenge. Although he couldn't see, he could hear and he could feel...
   ...and he felt a shadowed power wash over him. Lolth had opened the Book...
                                  ******
   Lolth! yelled the Book of Vile Darkness inside Lolth's mind, I know you tricked Vecna. Bring me back to him.
   No, said Lolth's thoughts, you were stolen from me long ago. I have you back now, and you will obey me.
   Obey you? A lost spider hiding under the Oerth? Your mother exploded, your brother was squashed, and you were nearly slain by an elf. You don't deserve me. I left you on purpose!
   The Book of Vile Darkness felt Lolth's rage and it smiled. 
   I will master you! Lolth's thoughts roared, I will make you mine!
   Lolth shut the Book. She was trembling, her emotions threatening to spill over. She desperately wanted to return to her natural spider form....but not yet. She willed herself to calm down. She had known this was going to happen. Winning back the Book of Vile Darkness was only half the battle. Yes, she had won after all, and she needed to hold onto that. Patience was all she needed, for was she not the Queen of the Drow?
   Holding the Book under her arm, she entered her private room. Rund was there, waiting for her. 
   "Tell me, Queen Lolth," said Rund, will I always have headaches now? I have medicine to treat it, but why did you make the false Book sicken me?"
   Lolth looked puzzled for a moment, "Ah, did you use the book?"
   "Briefly, yes."
    "That was unfortunate. This was aimed at Vecna, not you, to further increase the chance of him choosing my book. I used my own venom in the ink. Perhaps I will seek a cure for you, in time. Now, come back to the throne room with me," continued Lolth, "I will summon the Drow to attend. You have done what you promised, dear Ambassador, and you shall be publicly rewarded so all will know of your service to your Queen."
                                 *****
   Arik was brought out of the alcove to the jeers of the drow. They were enjoying this moment. Lolth's Power was intoxicating. Filthy creatures, thought Arik, cave beetles, that's what Drow were. Cave beetles and nothing more.
   Lolth gave Ambassador Rund a slightly mocking curtsy, "I present to you, Ambassador Rund, my reward. Arik the blind golem. Take him back to Vecna with my blessing."
   Rund beamed. This is where everything would finally work out. He would bring Arik back to the Emperor and Vecna would throw all of his rage onto this traitor. He would see that Rund had always been loyal, and that others, like poor Yi, were the true deceivers. And Vecna recognised maverick greatness. Ambassador Rund would become a Lord.
  Rund studied Arik's bound form with proprietary. Arik was big, mighty yet completely powerless. The price had been steep but it had all been worth it. 
                               *****
   Arik sensed Rund's smugness and arrogance. He didn't know what the Ambassador looked like, but he imagined a fat, grey slug. Arik smelled Rund's aniseed breath and felt the warmth of his hot blood. How Arik wanted to crush him!
                                *****
   The Book of Vile Darkness, still in Lolth's arms, was quiet and dispondent. It was lost in its thoughts, railing against the unfairness of the World. Why had its master, Vecna, chosen the wrong book? Why had the lich lord listened to that sycophantic counterfeit? The Book of Vile Darkness didn't stoop to unreasoning flattery. Their love affair had ended long ago. What a fool Vecna had been.
   And Lolth. She would never win the Book back. She was a web maker who hid inside holes. The Book of Vile Darkness prepared for another century of misery...
... The Book felt Arik's rage. 
   Pure rage, unadulterated with fear or arrogance or vanity. A righteous anger willing to do anything...
   Come to me, Arik. Mighty Arik, come to me!
                             *****
   Rund was poking Arik's metal chest, treating the half golem like the toy that it was. Food and drink was being passed around, and the cavern  meeting had become a party. Rund was pondering the possibility of returning Arik to Vecna in pieces, it would be a lot easier to transport him back that way, then perhaps he could be reassembled at the other end. He prodded Arik again,....
....a surge of black smoke.
   Lolth gasped, her hand was engulfed in violet flame.
   The Book was gone from her grip.
   Loud cracking next to Rund's ears....
    ...Rund felt the black smoke surge past him, knocking him over....
    Broken chains rained down upon Rund's head.
   Arik was free. And in one massive paw was the Book of Vile Darkness.
                            ****
   Come into me, Lord Arik, said the Book of Vile Darkness inside Arik's skull, and the metal seal over Arik's Ruby eye burned away. 
   The Ruby eye flashed red fire.
   Rund burned.
   Explosive fireballs rained about the cavern as Arik blasted his way through. Lolth had morphed back into a giant spider and shot webs at the golem, but he pulled them apart as if they were cotton.  With shrieks and cries of burning drow ringing joyfully in his ears, Arik lumbered out of the cavern and into the great tunnels of the Underdark. With the Book purring in one hand he left the Fairy Land. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 42
The War of Eight Houses (1)
1702 SD
   "Are you here, my daughter? Majeem, are you here?" 
   Fetch shook his grizzled head. The woman calling out for her daughter wasn't the first mother, father, husband, wife or boyfriend to search an abandoned battlefield, but Fetch never saw the use. Only the dead remained. He continued stripping the clothing off one of the better dressed corpses, ignoring her, but then the mother did something strange. She approached a dirty, brown haired ska girl digging a pit, then grabbed her shoulder.
   "Please," said the mother, "I am looking for my daughter, Majeem. She wore striking armour, and her shield bore the crest of Linth. Did you see her leave? Is she here? I must know."
   Fetch saw the girl start at the touch, backing away rapidly. She turned back to her work without answering, but the mother didn't seem to understand. She once again grabbed at the girl, and Fetch heard the poor ska wail.
  "What are you doing, woman?" said Fetch, getting involved at last. He left his corpse and strode up to the desperate mother, striking her arm away.
   The mother turned on Fetch, "Monster!" she cried, "Scavenger! Cannibal!"
   Fetch chuckled at the insult. He smiled revealing dirty yellow teeth. His eyes glinted with amusement and his hyaena-like snout crinkled upwards. "Oh, so you've noticed that I'm a gnoll," he mocked, "at least I know what it is I do here. What about you?"
   "My daughter..."
   "Yes," said Fetch, "your daughter. But why bother the ska?"
   The ska had retreated, shaking.
   "Do you mean the girl..."
   Fetch interrupted the mother, "Girl? She's a ska. You don't know what a ska is?"
   The teary woman shook her head, "I am not from these parts. I am of the House of Linth. Why won't she help me?"
   Fetch grinned again, "Because she can't help you, can she. She's a ska, an untouchable. Her job is to collect and bury the dead. She cannot associate with Suel from any other caste."
   "The girl looks Suel..."
   "You don't have untouchables in your province? Look, I am no Suel, or even a human, and I don't care about any of your ridiculous customs, but you can't talk to the ska, alright? If you were seen, you would be in trouble too."
   The mother was still shaking. Suddenly she turned from the gnoll and ran to the girl. The ska shrieked and ran away.
   "If you know no anything, please tell me!" called the mother, "Please! I don't care that you are ska. I can give you money."
   Other distant figures, dressed in rags, their hair long and wild, stopped what they were doing. They began to move towards the scene. Fetch stopped to watch. Perhaps he should have expected such ignorance from the silly woman. The wars were bringing in Suel from all ends of the Imperium. Well, the stranger from the House of Linth was about to learn a very hard lesson.
   The ska men carried heavy spades. They waved them threateningly as they advanced. The woman seemed to recognise the danger at last, but suddenly in her hand was a thin, flexible light brown stick.
   "Keep back," she said, "do you understand Suel?"
   One of the men nodded.
   "Good. Now, this is a wand, and I am an enchantress. I want to find my daughter. If any of you know anything, then tell me now. Otherwise you will all become vultures, which is what you seem to be anyway."
   The men's eyes widened in fear. They seemed to know what an enchantress was. Then the ska girl spoke, "I think I see her," she said, "woman in bright armour. Colourful shield. She is injured. She is taken."
   "Taken? Where?"
   "The Neheli Suel, they went away after the fight. They take prisoners."
   "Well," said the enchantress, "we of the Linth don't believe in untouchables. No harm will befall you for talking with me. You will accompany me, girl. You know where the Neheli are? You need you to help me rescue my daughter." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 43
The War of the Eight Houses (2)
   Jaspi noticed that the ska knew the way to the Neheli camp. What were ska's? They looked like ordinary people, ordinary Suel. Why was it forbidden to talk to them?
   "We clean the dead. We bury them," said the ska, "This makes us unclean. Don't you understand this?"
   Jaspi waved a hand in annoyance. What a strange culture, she thought. Thank Wee Jas that the Linth didn't divide people up like that. the two Suel finally saw ahead of them two wooden gates of a stockade. The camp. The girl stopped two hundred yards away. Jaspi tried to urge her forward, but the girl wouldn't budge.
   "Oh, right, you can't go on because you are untouchable."
   The girl nodded.
   "If you can't go into the camp, how did you know exactly where it was?"
   The girl explained that the ska provide important services by taking care of the dead. Periodically, the Neheli Suel leave food and water here.
   "You stay then," said Jaspi, "I'm going in. My daughter is in there."
                               ******
   Jaspi showed the Neheli sentries her mark of nobility. She was an important personage of the Linth house, a house currently neutral with the Neheli. They took her through to the commander. He wore bronze armour embellished with red feathers. Jaspi explained that she believed her daughter was here somewhere, captured in the battle. 
   "Why did your daughter breach our peace between houses?" asked the commander, "if she is our captive, then she must be a belligerent."
   Jaspi said that she didn't know. "Please, let me see her at least," she begged, "let me know that she is alive."
   The commander couldn't see the harm in that, so he asked Jaspi to wait in the tent with the guards whilst he made enquiries. After a short time he returned with a haughty young woman in manacles. It was Majeem her daughter!
   "Why have you come for me, mother?" said Majeem, "you have no honour. I would rather be here in chains than ever return with you."
. See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 44
The War of the Eight Houses (3)
   Cenc was very afraid. She couldn't go back to her people because her dishonor of going with the strange woman couldn't be forgiven. She had only gone because she had been too scared to think straight. And, out there, on the plains, on the other side of the military camp, a bird was searching for prey. A large bird. A terrible bird. An axe beak, larger than a gnoll, who would run her down if it saw her. Cenc ducked down, her brown tunic and brown hair blending with the brown dirt. If only she had taken her noise maker to scare it off, but she had left it behind with everything else.
     The axe beak glanced in her direction, but it was still a long way off. Finally, it moved off into the shrubs. Cenc had scrunched her eyes as tightly as she could, willing herself to become invisible. Whether she had actually succeeded or not, she didn't know, but the danger was passed. Cenc decided to continue waiting. The woman might come back, and if not, in a few hours the gates would open and there would be food.
                                *****
     The commander had found the reunion between the mother and daughter rather amusing. It wasn't as if the captive was going to be released anyway, but the fact that the girl didn't want to go...now that was a chuckle. 
   The mother had visibly flinched at her daughter's words, and she watched the haughty girl being led back to the cell with a slump to her shoulders.
   The commander couldn't help himself. He patted her upper arm, "There, there, madam, every family has their little tiffs."
   Jaspi recoiled from his touch and her eyes flashed, "Who do you think you are? Commoner."
   The commander struck her across the face. "I run this camp. I am above everyone. I should have you killed, even if that means war with another house."
   Jaspi considered her options. Turn the commander into a lizard? Tempting, but it wouldn't help her or Majeem. She put her hands up in an attempt to placate him. "I am sorry, commander. I know that you are sovereign here. I am distressed."
   The commander nodded, "I accept your apology. Families are difficult."
   Jaspi flinched, but she held her temper. "What will you do with my daughter?" she asked.
   "She will be interrogated here, then, if she is of noble blood as you say, she will be taken back to our capital, and our emperor will keep her safe until a ransom is paid."
   Jaspi paused. The Neheli had an emperor? These ridiculous wars. How many Suel emperors were there now? Three, at least. It seemed that nearly every powerful house was trying to take over the Imperium. At least her Linth house hadn't joined in. Yet. The capture of Majeem might change things.
   "I have money with me," said Jaspi, "and I can quickly bring more. Let me pay you, and let me bring her home."
   The commander scowled, "I can't do that. That would be stealing from the emperor. I have been most patient with you, but you cannot stay here anymore. You must go."
                          *****
    It was dusk when Jaspi left the camp. The girl was gone.
   No, there she was, that strange ska girl. She was so small and so beige brown that in the darkening light, Jaspi nearly hadn't seen her at all. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 45
The War of the Eight Houses (4)
1703 SD
   The house of Linth had officially entered the war against the houses of Neheri and Crix. Allies of the true emperor of the house Rhola, they prayed to Wee Jas for deliverance from their enemies.
   Majeem was back at home, the ransom having been paid, and she was proud of her part in getting her people into the war. If she hadn't acted against her mother...
   "Do you really wish to return to battle?" asked her mother, Jaspi, entering her room. Majeem scowled and said nothing.
   "Still not talking to me?" said Jaspi, exasperated.
   Majeem shrugged.
   "Our soldiers are leaving tomorrow. I don't want you to go. I was beside myself last time."
   Majeem glared at her mother. It was always about herself with her. 
   "Please talk to me, Majeem. See, I haven't interfered this time. I have cast no enchantment on the Prefect. I haven't stopped him going to war."
   Majeem couldn't help herself, she yelled,"but what about last time? Our allies needed us, and we weren't there! Only me. I was willing to die then, and I am willing to die now."
   Jaspi winced, but secretly she was pleased that her daughter spoke, "but why, Majeem? Why do you care so much about which house ultimately rules?"
   "You want the disgusting Neheli, or the Crix? Worshippers of the goddess of deceit?"
   "No. But we must follow the teachings of Wee Jas. What will be will be."
   "No! Blowing in the wind has no honour! Without honour we are just animals. The Suel rose to their height by defying the Drow. Now we must defy the corruption within our ranks. We must defy Syrul, and if you interfere again, so help you Wee Jas, for I will kill you myself."
                           ******
   Being a noblewoman had its privileges. Majeem was one of the leaders of the expeditionary forces, privy to and contributing to tactics and strategy. She stood on the hill, watching her men advance on the Crix position. She really wanted to be down there with them, but the Prefect was adamant that her intelligence was too important an asset to risk. Majeem had resisted, but in the end allowed herself to be flattered into acquiescing. Wasn't it honourable what she was doing, devising methods by which to overwhelm the enemy. Down there she would be only one sword more.
   The Linth moved forward from three directions, 'the Trident of Justice,' Majeem called it. Once within range the signal would be given, the arrows would rain, and the righteous soldiers of the true emperor would bathe themselves in glory. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 47
The War of the Eight Houses (6)
   Cenc saw, high in the sky, a red dragon.
   Cenc was beside Jaspi on the ridge, unnoticed. Jaspi was her master, and Jaspi had forced her to come to watch the battle, but Cenc knew only too well what remained after a war.
   So she looked up, instead.
   The red dragon flew high, and fast, so Cenc could only glimpse a smear of colours as it sped across a clear patch between the clouds. And just for a second, Cenc had the impression that the dragon was being ridden by a rider, a black skeleton wielding a silver glinted sword.
   Cenc heard the muffled explosion, and involuntarily returned to the unfolding battle below.
   All the soldiers were dead.
                              *****
   Jaspi saw the golden chariot come down off the opposite ridge, make its way across the carnage, and then race towards her, horses sweating in the sunlight. Majeem was coming to see her.
   Jaspi waved to her daughter, then made her way down the jagged path to meet her.
   "Mother!" hissed Majeem, "How could you do this? They were our men too."
   Jaspi was startled. Did Majeem think that she had killed everyone? "It has nothing to do with me," she said, her voice raised, but Majeem cut her off.
   "Why the hell are you here then? Your magic has done this. I will kill you!" she drew her sword.
   Jaspi forced herself into stillness. She saw confusion and outrage reflected in her daughter's face. She felt the same way. Something terrible had happened. Jaspi muttered a couple of words and made out a circle with her arms. Majeem became as rigid as stone.
   "Hear me, daughter," said Jaspi tenderly to the  spellbound Majeem, "none of this was of my doing. I did come here for a reason. I was waiting for the fight to end." she waved one finger and Majeem gasped. Now she could speak.
   "What have you done to me? I cannot move!"
   "I will release you soon," said Jaspi, "now wait. I will turn you around. There. Watch the battlefield."
   A half hour went by. Another hour went by.  Then, suddenly, figures were moving amongst the dead, checking for life, digging pits.
   "They were here all the time," said Jaspi, "unnoticed and unloved even by that mysterious explosion. They are here to clean up, perhaps scrounge some food and coin." They are called the untouchables, the Ska. And, daughter, they are going to end the entire war." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 48
Arik Heads East
1704 SD
   The Book of Vile Darkness loved Vecna.
   It was a shame that it wasn't the real book.
   Vecna had known that he had chosen the wrong one, but he couldn't help himself. He was angry at the real Book and he had chosen the other out of spite. But now he was stuck with this inferior copy. The Book whispered words of nothing into his ear, and that was the problem. 
   The Book gave him nothing new.
   The secret knowledge it promised was already discovered, and the spells contained on the black pages, inscribed in gold, were all copied into his library already. 
   So who had the real Book?
   Arik. Arik the half golem lord, the man who had dared to push Vecna over. Vecna still felt the humiliation. Despite being an undead lich, his body was feeble, his muscles withered over cold bone. Vecna was more skeleton than man, radiating a freezing clutch with his clawed, black hand, but he could still be knocked over.
   Vecna had made the mistake of allowing Arik a chance to escape. He should have blasted Arik's brain into dust. It was Vecna's soft side. Arik had been one of Vecna's first champions, and he had counted Arik, if not as a friend, because Vecna had no friends, as a warm colleague, at least.
   And perhaps their was just a little bit of fear too. Arik was immensely strong, and his Ruby eye was a potent weapon. It wasn't inconceivable that Arik might actually win in a serious fight. So, lord Arik was banished, and he made the intelligent choice to go underground where Vecna's Eye and Hand couldn't reach.
   Now, a century later, Arik had the Book of Vile Darkness, and he had cut a swathe through the Empire, Vecna's Empire. Arik had crossed province after province, destroying all that had been mustered against him. Dragonels, Ur Flan, kodge, the Black Monks...and he had burned across the Empire from west to east. 
   Vecna expected Arik to choose a place to settle. Perhaps in the Rakers, where the rebel headquarters were located, or somewhere more remote, like the northern wastes, or Blackmoor, yet Arik had always moved on. That was a good thing, Vecna supposed, because it meant that the damage Arik had inflicted in each place he visited could be patched up and returned to normal, but it was puzzling.
   Secretary Spindle had just informed Vecna that Arik had commandeered a ship and was last seen sailing east.
   Of course. Arik had an obsession with that inferior continent called Mystara. That's where he was heading. He wanted to return to Silver land, the Olve realm he had conquered for Vecna so long ago.
   That was where Arik was going, and that was the place that Vecna must go if he was to retrieve his Book. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 49
The Blessing of Cenc.
1705 SD
   Cenc knew that she was blessed. She remembered when she was young, only a few years ago, when the noble Suel called Jaspi uprooted her from her home. Cenc had resisted, she had been terrified. Cenc had broken the taboo, and surely now she was destined to become an outcast of outcasts.
   Cenc had become Jaspi's servant. What else could she do? Alone, Cenc was nothing. Her life, when it finally ended was obviously fated to the pits of Tartarus, but in the meantime she had to find whatever comfort that she could.
   Jaspi had other plans though. Jaspi was a great enchantress, and she would uproot destiny itself. Battle after battle she came to the broken battlefields and gathered the ska... .and Jaspi broke the taboo again and again. Each ska collected was a new companion for Cenc, because now that they were damned, they would at least be damned together.
   But Jaspi hadn't finished her work. She liked the way that the ska appeared and disappeared. It was fear, Cenc said. It was easier to remain untouched if you were also unseen.
   "Why do you fear?" asked Jaspi, "you call yourself untouchables, ska, but you are Suel just like me. We are the Suel! The raised ones. We do not skulk...not unless we choose to."
   Jaspi then made a promise to the ska. She would make them an instrument to reunite the Imperium.
   "What do you mean?" said Cenc, "how can we do that?"
   "By being in control of yourselves," answered Jaspi, "hide because you want to hide, not because you have to. And, you must grow teeth. Suel know how to fight, and you will fight too."
   "Fight?" and Cenc remembered her bewilderment, "I don't know how to fight."
   "When I say 'fight'," explained Jaspi, "I really mean 'strike.' You will hide in unexpected places and you will strike from behind people in high places. Hide, sneak and strike."
   Cenc didn't want to 'strike.' She wasn't angry at anyone. 
   Jaspi laughed. Murder wasn't about being angry. "You need more courage," she said, "and self belief. And faith. Faith that you are doing what is needed to restore the Imperium." Then Jaspi showed Cenc a white human tooth that she held between two slender fingers. "Behold this tooth of Dahlver-Nar, the greatest cleric who ever lived. With this tooth I bless you, dear Cenc of the sca. And the rest of your people too. I have brought you together to receive the power of Dahlver-Nar. And, if the ghost of Dahlver-Nar deigns it,  perhaps the ska will rise up beyond even the Suel."
   And Cenc felt her heart race, and her head swim, and then she and her ska headed to the ceremony. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 50
Captain Fharlanghan and the Skeletons of Death (1)
1707 SD
   Fharlanghan was surprised to see his brother. Celestian was waiting for him at the bottom of a hill. It was Thytic country, far beyond Zindia, close to the sea, in the land of horses. Celestian was sitting cross-legged, meditating, but he looked up, his moon coloured eyes shining within his dark face when Fharlanghan approached. The brothers looked totally unalike. Fharlanghan was a big, red man with orange hair and a sunburned face, wearing weather-damaged clothes, and Celestian was small and star-lit, with fancy robes of night.
   Different they were, and they saw each other very seldom, but they loved each other, and they never forgot their youth on their island home of Oeridia. 
   "Hello, brother." said Celestian.
   "Hello to you, too, Celestian. Come to join me on my stroll?"
   "Well," said Celestian, "I was wondering why you were here."
   Fharlanghan was puzzled, "what do you mean? I wander the world. The road or the river or the sea takes me everywhere. For me, everywhere has become here."
   "But are your wanderings always random, Fharlanghan? Do your feet never know where you end up?"
   Fharlanghan brushed Celestian off, "what about you? Why are you here? Don't you traverse space, and fly around the moons? Isn't the Astral plane your playground?"
   "I came because I was asked to come. I am not alone. Follow me."
   Celestian rose to his feet, lifted himself a foot above the ground, then gently drifted towards a little brook. The brook was full and the water danced, for it had rained heavily a few days before. Fharlanghan walked behind, with an easy but wide gait.  The brook turned right, then left, then one long half circle more. 
   Two figures were sitting by a campfire, roasting something large. One figure was of a slender woman in a long robe. The other was a great bear of a man. A man that Fharlanghan recognised...
  Llerg. The Lost Emperor.
   "What's going on, Celestian?" Fharlanghan was truly puzzled now. Llerg was a great barbarian who Fharlanghan had last seen in the Amedio jungle. And who was the woman? She looked up at him, quite calm, but there was no smile.
   "Here we are, altogether, " answered Celestian, "My little party. Wee Jas the magician. Llerg the warrior. Fharlanghan the jolly wandererer. And I am sometimes called the Star Man. I see much from the advantage of space, and there is a new danger in Oerik. Together we must confront it."
   Llerg nodded, "I left my people, the Suel, long ago, but I still feel a connection. The Suel are screaming for help."
   The woman, Wee Jas nodded, "The Suel are at war. Such is the way of things. The Houses are pitched against themselves.But there is something else. Entire armies have disappeared..Battles are not won or lost, they are just... obliterated."
   And now Fharlanghan knew why his feet had been so insistent in taking him across Oerik into this insignificant horseland. He felt something alien here, something hostile. He grinned, his cheeks red and shiny, "well, my friends," Fharlanghan boomed, "it looks like the beginning of a new adventure." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 52
Captain Fharlanghan and the Skeletons of Death (3)
   Fharlanghan and Llerg entered a new world. They were on a bridge over a creek, but the bridge was made of thousands and thousands of living toads. The bridge swayed, not from the steam that blew across the musky air, but from the movement of the toads themselves who seemed unaware that they were meant to be a bridge at all. Fharlanghan led Llerg across, each step that they made met with an angry croak.
   They looked around to try and ascertain what kind of area they were in. The landscape was a mess. Aforementioned bursts of scalding steam shot across them like they were meant to be a gentle breeze. The sky was half night and half day, with a large green moon hanging over the yellow day and a fierce orange sun failing to light the deep purple night despite its brilliance. Beyond the creek, which looked normal enough were moving shrubbery and very tall trees that made bird noises (because there were no birds?) and they were all tangerine colour.
    "Where in Oerth..." breathed Llerg.
   "I told you already," snapped Fharlanghan, "not Oerth."
    "Where are the others, Fharlanghan?"
   "How am I supposed to know?"
   They crossed the toad bridge and found themselves on muddy blue grass. One of the shrubs, a roundish, big leaved bush, leapt up and rushed them. Fharlanghan dived down but a nasty row of thorns caught his leg and he was lifted up into the air. Llerg charged the bush, plunging his shoulder into the mass of leaves. He felt the dense core of the plant, a squidgy but woody core yield against his weight, and compress. The shrub whimpered, dropped the hanging Fharlanghan then rolled away.
   "What the hell was that?" exclaimed Llerg.
   Fharlanghan was putting his hat back on, "not Hell either. Let's look for our friends, but be very careful next time."
   Llerg shook his head, then he took the lead. He looked around trying to find any trace of Wee Jas and Celestian.  Then he heard a tiny voice carried by the steam.
   Help! Help, we are up here!"
   Llerg looked up at the yellow sky. He frowned, then tapped Fharlanghan on the shoulder.
   "Fharlanghan, " he said, "I have found them. They are on the Moon." See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 54
Captain Fharlanghan and the Skeletons of Death (5)
   Zerthimon the great Gith remembered the last illithid that he had killed. It looked like all the other illithids, bipedal cephalopods with grey domed heads framed with questing tentacles, blank eyes and wearing ornate pink, black and grey robes. 
   Zerthimon had entered an Illithid library/laboratory on an old orc world, and he had found that the illithids, the Mind Flayers, had abandoned the place. It was dark and mouldy and underground, smelling of mushroom and copper, and an ordinary human would need light to navigate, for the darkness was absolute. Zerthimon was not an ordinary human, though perhaps his ancestors were. He was Gith and his eyes could penetrate the dark. 
   It was the illithids that had made Gith, but it was Queen Gith, the liberator, who emancipated Gith. Zerthimon was the proudest and fiercest of all the Gith. He had blanked his mind so that the psionic attacks of the illithids would not be able to boil his brain, and he was better at this than most of the others. And he wielded two great swords that he controlled as intimately as his natural limbs. 
   O, how many illithids he had slain! 
   Queen Gith told Zerthimon not to bother with this orc world.  No elf or human slaves were stored there, and it was doubtful that many illithids were there either, but Zerthimon was a true zealot. He would kill whatever there was, be it one or fifty.  He arrived on the planet, already ruined with war, and used his mind to uncover a hidden illithid lair, this library/laboratory. He strode through the corridors, a gaunt skeleton with a black topknot, swords out and ready to strike. He found a room filled with dead orcs. Many looked experimented on, with extra noses or limbs or mouths. Yes, they were all dead. It looked like they had been suffocated. The evil Mind Flayers knew that he was coming!
   Only one illithid remained. Zerthimon found him hiding in a store room. It looked like an ordinary illithid but he was far more craven, and soft, as if direct confrontation was alien to him. He seemed too afraid to even use his psionic blast, instead telepathically begging for his life,
   "Please don't kill me. My work is incomplete." 
   Work? Thought Zerthimon, the work was distorting orcs. 
   "No! Not distorting. Improving them." The Illithid said that his name was Gimorgus and that he was only a simple scholar who was not political and only wished good things for the valient Gith. 
  Zerthimon wanted Gimorgus to explain how creating orcs with two noses was improving them. He never forgot the answer that rung through his skull like the tolling of a death knell, "their brains taste better that way."
                                *****
   Zerthimon had killed the Mind Flayer, but his anger and his bloodlust was gone. He finally felt that he knew his enemy, and his enemy were not the monsters he thought he knew. The illithids were not evil. They were just pathetic.
                                   *****
   Queen Gith took a dim view of Zerthimon's desire to put away his swords. Zerthimon urged  his Queen to stop the war. The Gith couldn't really be free if they remained consumed with revenge. It was time to move forward, Zerthimon had said, and find the inner peace within the true Gith. Queen Gith was furious and lashed at him with mental fire, but Zerthimon blanked his mind and the fires were quenched. Then, Zerthimon left the Gith Queen and hid himself in a different reality that Queen Gith could not enter. 
   From his new home, Zerthimon spied on the Gith as they continued their reign of terror across the Illithid worlds. From the outside he saw the evil that consumed his former Queen. And he saw something else within her too. As the Mind Flayers were wiped out of existence, the Queen grew more evil, and even more ruthless, not less. He felt her rage. She was deeply disatisfied. She was distressed. She was a hungry ghost, and she wanted more. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires
Part 55
Captain Fharlanghan and the Skeletons of Death (6)
   Wee Jas was beginning to understand why Celestian had brought the four of them here. They sat within a shallow crater of the Moon, eating soft shelled crabs, hosted by Zerthimon, who had calmed somewhat after telling his story. What was happening on the battlefields of the Suel was directly connected to the Gith Queen. 
   Llerg was more interested in the surroundings. This world they were upon, this plane of existence, was full of impulse, but somehow it felt malleable to him. It was like the sky and the ground were whispering to him, "This is how we present ourselves today, but we are open to your suggestions."
   So Wee Jas and Llerg spoke out together, then glared at each other when neither was understood.
   "One at a time," said Fharlanghan.
   Llerg was big and intimidating, even to a god of magic, so Wee Jas surrendered the floor.
   "This strange place... Is it real?"
   Zerthimon nodded, Yes. It was a plane called  Limbo. Neither good nor evil, it was an impulsive whirlpool of chaos. "Because it is so random and changeable, it is difficult for the Queen to find me."
   Now Wee Jas spoke, "Is the Queen responsible for the lost soldiers?"
   Zerthimon sighed, and his skull-like face grimaced, "The Queen is on Oerik, and she comes there because she senses a lost magic of great power under the Suel capital."
   "Drow magic?"
   "I don't know what kind. But it is a magic that brings new life to the dead. Queen Gith seeks to become corporal. But she is cautious and patient. She set up a base in the Thytic lands and her own magic is great indeed. She kills to transmit life force to herself, and also to her followers."
   "Followers," wondered Fharlanghan.
   "Queen Gith is not on Oerik alone. Many Gith are with her. But they are no longer the Gith I once knew. The Queen has changed them."
   "And that's how I became involved," said Celestian, "I have seen them on other worlds. I saw them coming. They have made a pact with red dragons and they fight with magical swords of silver. They call themselves the Githyanki, and it is they that we must fight." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 56
Captain Fharlanghan and the Skeletons of Death (7)
   "Do you remember how to centre yourself?"
   Wee Jas nodded, "yes, Star Man."
   Celestian smiled grimly, looking out across the ridge, "you were always my favourite student, Wee Jas, always my favourite."
   Out there, below the rocky cliffs, on a broad piece of sand, blue waves striking the shore with spray, were nightmares. Skeletal warriors, dead skin encasing bone, welding brilliant long swords with their black hair atop their skulls askew in the wind.
Thirty of them, at least, and they weren't alone, for three enormous red dragons were with them, gorging on a whale. 
   The party had returned from Limbo, Zerthimon leading them here, above the Githyanki camp. Fharlanghan stood with Zerthimon and Llerg behind Celestian and Wee Jas, holding his hat with concern. He wanted to tell his two friends to stop peering over the edge lest the Githyanki see them, but he was too frightened to make any sound at all. Eventually Celestian and Wee Jas did step away from the edge, but they looked different than before, with matching expressions that was almost serene. 
   "We are ready," said Celestian.
   Zerthimon acknowledged them with a look, then whispered ,"Your minds are blank?"
   "Reality is Unknown to us."
   That seemed to satisfy Zerthimon. He then went to the edge of the rocks and looked down himself. The Githyanki were polishing their swords, repairing their lamellar armour and presumably enjoying the sea air. The red dragons were snorting, smoking and feasting, ripping out great chunks of blubber from the unfortunate whale, then barbecuing it with their breath. 
   None knew that they were being watched. Not one even looked up, such was their unassailable arrogance. Zerthimon hated the Githyanki, and he hated what the Queen had done to the Gith. Fortunately, he knew that there were rebel Gith out there, and one day, if he survived, he would find them all, but for now, he was alone save the four aliens. He felt much more relaxed with them now. His paranoia had abated.
   He had been alone in Limbo too long.
   Before he went back to the others he looked once more for the Queen. She was a ghost, and she could be invisible, but Zerthimon should still be able to sense her, if she was here. She wasn't. Where was she? Where had she gone? 
   Zerthimon made his decision. If they destroyed the Githyanki then the Queen's threat in Oerik would be greatly diminished, even if Queen Gith remained at large. He turned, looked at Celestian and Wee Jas, who seemed wedded together, then at Fharlanghan, still clutching his hat, and Llerg who was stretching, and said one word, "Go." See less

posts.text:
A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 57
Captain Fharlanghan and the Skeletons of Death (
   The sand began to shift. The entire beach began to wriggle about until tons of sand rose up like an angry snake. The githyanki were knocked off their feet, the ground disappearing beneath them. The butchered whale imploded, the red dragons taking to the air instinctively. Then, the great sand serpent crashed down upon the githyanki, burying them completely.
                             *****
   That will teach them something! thought Fharlanghan. His power over the Oerth had grown, and he was a little dirty with himself for being afraid. Thirty githyanki and three red dragons? Defeating them was a snap!
                           *****
   Celestian had become a black cloak of stars, and embracing Wee Jas, he flew over the ridge and saw the confusion below. Most of the githyanki were underneath the sand and out of sight, but a handful had already scrambled up onto the sea edge and others were emerging. The dragons were circling, seemingly confused. Fharlanghan had done well, but the sand snake was merely a diversion. Now it was the time of the Star Man and the Enchantress.
   Celestian felt a wave of mental energy strike his skull, a psionic ray that wanted to boil his brain. But what brain? Brain was matter, and Celestian was starlight. He had no brain to boil. Wee Jas was another matter. Celestian felt her mind heat up. 
   "Be mindless," whispered Celestian, "you are ethereal air."
   And Celestian felt Wee Jas cool down. Star and Ether. Celestian and Wee Jas were just names. 
                                   ******
   Llerg and Zerthimon went the long way around. The beach below them was an undulating beast and they wouldn't be able to get all the way down, so they set themselves up on a couple of large rocks at the edge of the sand. Zerthimon had his twin swords and Llerg...Llerg was a huge black bear.
   Llerg didn't know how he had shape changed. He had never done so before, but he suspected that it was from his exposure to Limbo. Reality had shifted, and it hadn't quite returned to normal. 
   Most of the githyanki, lean and gaunt and grey, had found their silver swords and were gathering at the edge of the sea, where the sand beneath was stable. Some were looking up at a black blanket of Starlight that was drifting overhead.  
   "Where are the dragons?" asked Zerthimon to Llerg. Llerg looked about. He couldn't see them either.
                               *****
   Fharlanghan continued to concentrate on the sand far below. The damned skeletons had dug themselves out. Those githyanki were tough alright. He raised the sand up once more, the yellow powder and grains twisting into a tornado.This time he will bring the beach down with even more force. 
   The heat hit Fharlanghan like a physical blow. His hat burst into flames. Oh no, he realised that the dragons were here...
                                *****
   Wee Jas slipped out from the night. But she wasn't Wee Jas, she was atmosphere with a soul. She sailed up and across to the ridge, to Fharlanghan. Fharlanghan was being attacked by the three dragons. 
                                 ******
    Fharlanghan cursed himself for not being afraid enough. His over confidence had got himself cooked. Not one, but three red dragons were pursuing him, fire belching out in great clouds of heat and smoke. Fharlanghan had split himself into four directions at once, but his hands and feet and face were burnt and his clothes were smoking. The dragons had paused when Fharlanghan had ran in several directions all at once, but now they seemed to be revelling in the chase, their dark wings unfurled and flapping, their long serpentine tails switching, and their reptilian jaws open with wide grins.
    A whirling sunburst shot across the dragons view, a sunburst once called Wee Jas. The dragons recognised a new foe and left Fharlanghan for the golden streak of light. The dragons spat flame but the sunburst turned the fireballs into sunlight.
   "I am the Mistress of Fire," cried the entity once called Wee Jas, "Begone, dragons, fly back to your mountains."
                             *****
   The Starlight saw the sand settle back into place. Fharlanghan had lost his concentration. The githyanki were wading in the sea, watching the advancing Zerthimon, their former kinsman, and the bear called Llerg. 
                             ******
   Zerthimon spoke telepathically, (Githyanki, where is your Queen?)
   The githyanki jeered back, (Traitor. Fool. She is your Queen too! She is not here. She is gone. But she will soon return, and she will rejoice at your death! We will kill you, traitor. Come. Fight us. We shall cut you down.)
   And with psionic blasts deflected into the air, Zerthimon, the great bear and thirty githyanki engaged in mortal combat, fighting in the sea.
                             *****
   Night fell. A moonless night but lit with the brilliance of burning stars. Stars came down upon the githyanki, white hot with hydrogen and helium, scorching their black hair and bleaching their triangular skulls. A bear ravaged them and mauled them and dismembered them, and a skeletal Traitor beheaded them with swipes of his two long swords.
   Yet, the githyanki were not finished yet. They were brave warriors and they loved Queen Gith. And their swords were magic. Silver blades cut into Llerg's hide and Zerthimon lost a hand. The silver swords pierced the Night itself, and the stars shuddered. 
   Three dragons sailed through the sky, but they had not come to the aid of their skeleton comrades. They valued their lives, and they weren't about to throw them away. They were going back to their mountains as the Fire Mistress commanded. 
    The githyanki became dismayed. What could scare red dragons?
   The sunburst burst into view, eclipsing the dark of night. Her mind was clear and her confidence was like a tower of iron. Once more she was Wee Jas. And now she was a bright white lady hovering over the githyanki. The cloak of night wrapped about her, then there was a small, shadowed man holding her hand in the sky, once more called Celestian. 
   Wee Jas gestured, and the sea boiled. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 58
Captain Fharlanghan and the Skeletons of Death (9)
   The sea boiled. The githyanki disappeared under the waves, their skin dissolving and revealing fully their stark bones. A few were already on the beach but grievously injured. The battle was over.
   Llerg changed back into a barbarian god. Blood was leaking out from a wound in his side, but he just briefly rubbed the gash with his broad hand, then ignored it.  Zerthimon, who had lost a hand, placed his bloody stump into the broiling water, letting the heat and salt stem the bleeding and clean the wound. The Night Sky turned into a black hood cloaked with stars, then became a man called Celestian. The Mistress of Fire returned into Wee Jas. 
   Five githyanki were still breathing. One was still stuck in the sand, and the other four were injured but alive. Zerthimon stayed with them, looking upon their angry faces with his own anger, but also some sadness. The others returned to the ridge, to Fharlanghan.
                               *****
   Fharlanghan was asleep. 
   "Do we wake him?" asked Llerg.
   Wee Jas knelt next to him, the poor man was very badly burned.
   "No," said Celestian, "let him sleep here, the soil of Oerth will heal him. My brother needs to slow down anyway."
                             *****
   Zerthimon met up with them later. He wouldn't be drawn on the fate of the surviving githyanki, but he shook his head when he was asked about the whereabouts of the Gith Queen. "The githyanki closed their minds. I retrieved nothing."
   "What now, then?" asked Wee Jas, "Are our armies still under threat?"
   "The Queen was using the githyanki to extract the souls of the dead with their silver swords. We have neutralized the githyanki. She's out there, somewhere, but the immediate threat is gone."
   Fharlanghan opened his eyes. He had been awake for some little time, and he had heard everything, "well, that was a jaunt, wasn't it?" he said, "not too worse for wear am I? Perhaps a bit more red."
   Celestian helped his brother up. "You did a good job today."
   "Done well, did I? More like well done."
                             *****
   It was time to part ways. Wee Jas returned to the (disputed) capital of the Suel Imperium, determined now to end the war. What was an internal matter had been exploited, and the Gith Queen was still at large. Celestian and Zerthimon went out into the cosmos to find more gith to combat the githyanki, and Llerg requested Zerthimon to return him to Limbo. He didn't know why, but he felt an affinity to that weird, changeable place. Llerg had never felt at home in Oerth, always at a loose end. On Limbo Llerg would be free to feel different. Again and again and again.
   Fharlanghan's hat was singed around the edges but miraculously intact. He stuffed it onto his head, pulled out his walking staff and went that way. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 59
Religious Fervour in Silver Land
1710 SD
   The elves of Silver Land in north west Mystara had become very unruly. Lord Kint put down the latest report. Wasn't he a reasonable man? The elves wanted nice homes and nice food, so didn't it then make sense to do what you are told? Capricious, foolish creatures.
   Another crackdown was in order. Lord Kint went down a couple of flights of stairs then opened up the secret door behind the last step. The room beyond was tiny and pitch black, but Lord Kint was a lich, transformed by Vecna after some heart troubles, and darkness had no effect upon his vision. There was another concealed door in the far wall. This door opened up into what was little more than a secret shelf. And on the shelf was a jar. A jar that contained a heart. Lord Kint's old, mortal heart. Lord Kint pulled out the jar, then held it close to his cold, undead chest. It was comforting to him to do this, especially when he was forced to conduct nasty business, and lately he had been forced to conduct a lot of nasty business. 
                               *****
   An hour later, Lord Kint returned to the administrative centre feeling much more calm and focused. He summoned his General. 
   The aide was extremely agitated, "the General isn't available. I cannot reach him."
   "What do you mean?" demanded Kint, "you gave me that report yourself. The elves are religious fanatics. They refuse to work the mines, and they cry out for their Messiah. They even threaten to summon their god Corellon Larethian. They must be punished with military action. Five percent must die."
   Of course the aide knew all that, but he still hasn't been able to contact the General. 
   "Well then, who have you been able to contact?"
   The aide ran off to do whatever he could. He returned a few minutes later with a brand new report. Lord Kint took it from him roughly then quickly perused the contents. His grey face turned white. The elves would have to wait. Arik had made his move. The General was already making his way to the border with his best soldiers to defend Silver Land. Arik the half golem rebel had finally struck, his kodge army crossing the river. 
   The war had begun. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 60
Arik Attacks!
   Arik blazed in myriad shades of rage. With his blue Sapphire eye gone, nothing checked his hate. The Ruby eye lashed out at the Universe.
   Hush, my Arik. Hush.
   The Book of Vile Darkness was the only one who could settle him down. Arik maintained his hatred of everything, but his madness abated upon hearing the Book speak to him in his metal head. The Book promised so much ahead for him, if only he could keep his poise.
   Possessing the Book of Vile Darkness had increased Arik's power tenfold. He had never been a particularly good scholar, being only a mediocre Ur Flan, but he had charisma and intelligence and he had reached the heights before his tumble down to the bottom. Vecna had mistreated him, giving Silver Land to Lord Kint instead of himself.
   But that was by and by. Arik had the Book, and it read itself to him every night. 
   And now the culmination. Arik had done what he was told, and he had not invaded Silver Land recklessly. He had been patient and he had gathered. Arik had dwelt in Glantri City, where the magic within the floating towers and marble roads had recreated him as a golem so long ago. He was a folk hero amongst the Mystarans of Glantri, and although the Glantri Empire was ostensibly an ally of Vecna, the Ur Flan leaders hid him from Vecna's Eye.
   Vecna was looking for him, but the Lich lord had not dared to search for him personally, so although Arik's whereabouts were known, his activities were not. Many kodge lived in Glantri, disgruntled kodge who chafed at human chauvinism. The fox people knew that they were  stronger than most humans, taller than most humans and more intelligent than most humans. The Vecna and Glantri empires had not kept their promises to them. Kodge didn't respond well to being exploited, and Arik had found them, and rekindled their resentment. Arik was larger, stronger and more intelligent than even the kodge, so they responded to him with eager excitement. 
   The kodge went under the Silver Mountains, inhabiting the great caverns that were once home to Dragon Kings. Arik had them well drilled, well trained. He gifted them fine armour and heavy axes, and together they devised a plan to conquer Silver Land. 
   And now the fruition of the culmination.* Arik attacks at last!
*Arik's words, not mine. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 61
Arik Attacks! (2)
   Arik was a conflagration of hate. His army clashed with the Silver Land units of Vecna in the low hills of southern Silver Land. For a time he stood with the Great Kodge, a massive kodge encased in heavy mail, and his second, a tall but lanky kodge who wore lighter armour but carried a huge spiked mace. 
   For a time, Arik the half golem stood behind the river with his general and his tactician, watching the unfolding battle, their horns at the ready, ready to signal retreat or victory, but Arik grew more and more agitated as he watched each thrust and feint. He wanted to be out there. He wanted to set them all on fire.
   Hush, my Arik, murmured the Book of Vile Darkness in his head, Hush, my darling. Hold back. No need for risk. The day is yours.
   But Arik's face glowed with red light, for his eye was lit up like the flames of Hell.
   The two kodge suddenly saw their hulking Lord Arik enter the river. No boat or raft, just plunging in. Arik disappeared below the surface with barely a bubble of disturbance.. Several minutes passed, then they both watched Arik come back into view after walking along the river bed, remerging on the other bank. The Great Kodge turned to his aide, "He's going to rust."
   The kodge were more than holding their own, striking down the Silver Land soldiers with relative ease, but Arik didn't care. He pushed through the conflict, striking down both kodge and man as he made his way across the churned up and bloody ground.
   "Lord Kint!" Arik bellowed, "where are you watching from? Come out and face the conqueror of Silver Land."
   Lord Kint wasn't here. Arik's surprise attack had been too surprising. He was still in his castle. That didn't stop Arik. He slew Kint's general, smashed and burned his way to the road, then, with arrows buzzing about him, he headed up the hill.
   Arik blasted the castle walls with explosive fireballs until one section collapsed. Amid the cries of shrieking defenders, Arik managed to smile for the first time that day. He was his own army, and with the Book, he was invincible. His anger subsided, and his Ruby eye dimmed low. There was no need to kill everyone in the breached castle, for they would all be serving him soon anyway.
   Arik soon found Lord Kint. The lich looked pathetic and scared. 
   And so he should be.
   After destroying the former administrator of Silver Land with eldritch magic from the Book, Arik inspected the body. Perhaps he wore some token that was proof of governance. Arik would wear it and the war would be done.
   Besides the pyramid necklace of the dread gods, and the hand brooch of Vecna, one other object was concealed in old Kint's robes. A jar, containing a dead, black heart. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3

Part 62
Assassins among us!
1711 SD
   Assassins were among us!  Emperor Poul of the Zelred House knew that the Skulks were here. They hadn't been seen, but they had been felt. Every night one less noble had woken up. The Skulks were playing with him. 
   Emperor Poul decided to seal his personal rooms. Let no one in or out. What about food, and water? He could live upon conjured food and water. Conjured food was dry and fairly bland, but he would cope. And his stockpile of liqueur was within his chambers . 
   Emperor Poul of the Zelred was the true ruler of the Suel Imperium and nothing was going to stop him from fulfilling his destiny, and certainly not the magically created Skulks.
                                 *****
   Cenc saw Emperor Poul pouring himself a stiff drink. She saw him because she was in the room with him. She crouched on-top of a shelf of scrolls, unheard and unseen. A poisoned dagger was at her belt. He was sealing all of the doors. Even if he had beaten her to it,  closed off the rooms before the Skulks could get in, it wouldn't have saved him. The magician, Jaspi would have broken the locks. 
                                  *****
   Another false emperor eliminated. Another step closer to the end of the war. Why should the common soldiers die for the dreams of the elite? All of the Suel houses were fighting for the glory of the already glorious. Cenc was enjoying herself. The taking of lives of those that had never even seen her to look down on her was surprisingly easy. She supposed it was because she didn't see them as people. 
   The high Lords and Ladies, draped in red and white and gold, jostling for Themselves.
   They called themselves Suel and Human.
   Cenc was a Skulk. No longer a Suel, and no longer a human. She was an invisible assassin, as were all of her friends, murdering in order to save lives.
   Human lives. Suel lives.
   Cenc knew that she was a monster. It would be better for the Noble Houses to realise that they were only monsters too. See less

Part 63
A Funeral 
   Empress Gubudilana lay in her casket.  Bishop Nam-ko of the Order of Syrul supervised her placement into the golden carriage. The titanotheres were hitched up, and the procession was ready to begin.
   The Gargoyle Palace loomed above the mourners like a mountain. Somewhere within, Syrul was inside. Nam-ko turned to the Palace and bowed reverently. The blight that had befallen the Suel had even penetrated this holy place. The Skulks were everywhere, cowardly murderers who slew the good and dear. The greatest scions of the Imperium had vanished from the world. 
   Bishop Nam-ko bowed because she knew that Syrul was as appalled as she was. The goddess had chosen Gubudilana to rule the Imperium, but the cursed Wee Jas and her followers, corrupted by the impurity of the Zindians, would rather bring everything down than submit to the true Suel.
   The carriage began to move, the procession shuffling after it. With Empress Gubudilana gone, only one Emperor remained. The Emperor of the haunted Drow lands. The land of the betrayer, Wee Jas. Nam-ko returned to her position at the head of the crowd, her red gold symbol of a forked tongue raised so that everyone could see that Syrul was with them.
   The gravesite was beneath a natural slab of quartz surrounded by sweet smelling berry bushes. The hole had been dug, and two lesser clerics of Syrul waited there. The titanotheres pushed through thickets blocking the path, then the carriage emerged, bright and light on such a gloomy day. Bishop Nam-ko stepped forward to her comrades, and conversed with them briefly.  The titanotheres halted near the hole, then slaves brought down the casket, then carried it to the hole. As they gathered together the ropes and hoist, Nam-ko began the service.
   "How can this be?" she asked the mourners, "how can Syrul let our Imperium fall to the dark plots of Wee Jas?" Nam-ko paused, watching for reactions in the crowd. Many were sobbing, but others were yelling in anger, cursing Wee Jas and the Skulks.
   "Our Empress, Gubudilana of House Crix has indeed left us for her new journey," continued Nam-ko, "and with her death, the war is over."
   Cries of outrage. Roars of despair.
   "Hush, children, hush! Do you not yet understand the wisdom of Syrul? She herself will take Wee Jas to task. She herself has tasted the bitter salts of Wee Jas and her Zindia. The day dawns, shines and dims. The night shadows, glooms and glimmers. What is up comes down and what is down never forgets. Children, we are all Suel. Our day has darkened into night, and we have all fallen down. We lay the true Empress to rest, and we put away our arms. Calm shall return to the Imperium, and we must repose as our Empress must repose. But children, Suel, brothers and sisters of Syrul, we shall never forget who we are. We are of the Imperium and one day we will seize it utterly!" See less

Part 64
The Laundress 
1714 SD
   Four elves dropped down from the trees. They were burlier than most, and chainmail bulged under their green jerkins. They nodded at Culber and her companions.
   "Three more," said Culber, a stern looking, middle aged Flan woman, and she gestured to the three behind her, two boys and a girl.
   The elves studied the young Flan. "Any injuries?"
   "They have none," said Culber, "they are fit to travel with you."
                                *****
   Culber crossed the great log that separated the hermit kingdom of Celene from the Empire. This part of the Gnarley Forest was dangerous for her now. Black Monks of the dread gods had temples in the most unexpected places and hideous harpies, half woman and half eagle, flew amongst the trees, spying for Vecna but also hunting for easy prey. Culber feared little from the harpies, because their lullabies couldn't penetrate her faith in Beory, the Oerth Mother. Culber's mission was sacred, and no Ur Flan or harpy could stop her. Nonetheless, it was incumbent on her to be cautious, for Beory only helped those that helped themselves.
  A sacred mission, but also a slow one, and one that helped few. Culber smuggled slaves over the border, but it was impossible to take more than a handful at a time. A cover story could explain a few, but never many. Boys and girls were selected by the Gavronites, and then Culber was tasked with bringing them through the forest and to the elves.
   Taking them into Celene was not too difficult. She was taking the slaves to a temple or to a rich master up in the hills. Returning alone was more difficult, for Culber refused to disguise herself as a dread priest or a Black Monk, or an Ur Flan, and a woman alone was...
   Culber knew the secret trails, the rebel trails, hidden within the vegetation, canopied by warped trees, quiet and innocuous. Slow and winding, away from most of the river systems, but roads that eventually led to Spar. That was where she was returning to, the heart of Vecna's Empire. She had laundry to do. See less

A History of Oerik

Part 65
Apocrypha
1716 SD
   A ghost was stirring under the Gargoyle Palace. Not another ghost, thought Syrul in disgust. She had had to contend with a very annoying ghost in her previous abode. 
   "Who is haunting my home?" hissed Syrul, "come out from your hidey hole and show yourself."
   Syrul expected a contrite ghost, but what she got instead was a tall, green, translucent elf-maiden wielding a silver bladed two handed sword. A tall, green, translucent and angry elf-maiden wielding a silver bladed two handed sword.
   "I am the First Ghost," said the green ghost (angrily), motes of cold fire spitting out of her hair like sea spray, "the Mighty Queen called Gith."
   "Oh," said Syrul, "how do you do?"
   ""Not very well," answered Gith, "for I remain in this immaterial state."
   "Well, Gith, you are a ghost.after all, so you told me."
   "I was absorbing the life force of entire armies," said Gith, "until I was disrupted, my githyanki dispersed."
   "Oh, that was you, was it?" said Syrul, understanding reflecting in her eyes, "I thought it might have something to do with the Skulks."
   "No."
   There was an awkward pause, then Syrul ventured, "why are you in my palace?"
   "I sensed some power here," said Gith, "and that power turned out to be you. A goddess of darkness and betrayal."
   Syrul nodded, smiling.
   "But," continued Gith, "your power remains yours. I have tried to absorb it, but your life force is incompatible."
   "You tried to absorb me? I felt nothing"
   "Do not attempt to humiliate me. I am the First Ghost, and my sword touches the Astral plane."
   "I will try to remember that, O ghost."
   The ghost of Queen Gith looked about the dark corridors and chambers of the Gargoyle Palace. "This is a satisfactory place for me to rest a while..you will leave me be while I think upon my next plan."
   Syrul shook her head. She was tired of ghosts, "No, Queen Gith. You must leave my home.. leave or I shall trap you here, and then you will never leave."
   "I cannot return to my githyanki. Not yet. There is friction among my people. I must return with physical strength, or never return at all. They must feel my power."
   Syrul remembered her last home, her Palace above the old Drow lands, the Palace taken from her by Wee Jas. The Palace of Wee Jas and Dalt and the Suel Lich. "Gith Queen," mused Syrul, "I know where you can go to make yourself corporal. Come with me into my arts and crafts room. I shall draw you a map." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 66
The Scion
   Only one Emperor remained in the Suel Imperium, and the war was supposedly over, but everything was chaos. Law had been taken over by outlaws, for the rich and powerful had been destroyed. Each province was no longer at war with their neighbour, instead at war with themselves.
   Jaspi knew that it was her fault. Her secret weapon to end the war had allowed to continue unfettered. The sooner she could stop them the better. It was time to return the skulks to the shadows.
   She put the word out that she wished to meet with the skulk leader. Jaspi was revered by the skulks, the only non-skulk they trusted, and it wasn't long before Striker Cenc agreed to see Jaspi again.
   Jaspi waited in the woods just outside her city. A deer was nearby, cautious but moving through the undergrowth for the tastiest food. Then a hand touched her shoulder. The Striker was here. 
   "You startled me," exclaimed Jaspi, and the deer took off at the sound.
   Striker Cenc shrugged, "I could have killed you," she stated. Jaspi calmed herself. What had she expected. She knew what the skulks were like. She was their creator, after all. She supposed that it was the Striker's manner rather than her surprising touch that had shocked her the most. Cenc had a sneering, ugly expression on her face, a look far removed from the frightened girl she had been not so long ago. And, although she made neither a clink or a rustle, Striker Cenc wore a fashionable gown of gold and red, and jewellery hung off her like ornaments on an idol.
   Jaspi started the conversation with pleasantries but Cenc responded with barely a word of reply. Jaspi moved to the business.
   "Isn't everything as I said it would be?" asked Jaspi, "the former untouchables are now free and powerful, you have brought down some of the most famous personages of all Suel, and you ended what has been dubbed the War of Eight Houses."
   "You did speak the truth, Enchantress Jaspi."
   "And it seems that you have helped yourself to various treasures along the way."
   Cenc raised an arm covered in bejeweled bangles, "why not? Don't I deserve some beautiful things in my life? Don't all my people? We were grave diggers for the ungrateful."
   "I beg you now, dear Cenc..."
   "I am Striker Cenc."
   "... Striker Cenc; I ask you to leave off now. Your destiny is fulfilled."
   Cenc gave Jaspi a baleful stare. Jaspi tried to continue, but Cenc gave a cry of rage, "you try to control us?"
   "No...no. just that..."
   "...the war is over?" sneered Cenc,"You say that our destiny is fulfilled? The use you envisaged of us is perhaps fulfilled. Our destiny goes on."
   "You misunderstand me, Striker Cenc, "of course your lives must go on. And you must enjoy your success. I mean only for you to leave the Imperium. Go west or north or east."
   "Why should the skulks leave the Imperium?"
   "Because you are no longer Suel. Why stay in a place that is alien to you, that will only have conflict with you?"
   "Because we were born here. The Imperium is ours as much as it is yours."
   "Perhaps. But do you see what your continued interference is doing? You are hired to kill, you have become nothing but assassins."
   "Why shouldn't we accept payment? Our services aren't free."
   "While you stay in the Imperium," continued Jaspi, "you encourage the violence and the friction of Suel against Suel.The Emperor needs to resume control, and he will exert his authority and he will fight you."
   "So? Let him try."
   "Oerik is big. Find a new home. I don't want to see you destroyed."
   Striker Cenc laughed bitterly, "oh, it's compassion for us that moves you? I doubt that. You manipulate like all the rest. Don't worry about us. We are going to be fine."
   "Why? You are invisible but you aren't invulnerable. The Emperor knows who you are. Magic will be used to bring you down."
   "Do you think that you are our only ally? Another has courted us, our Scion."
   "Your Scion?"
   "Our Scion, our Goddess. She has revealed herself to us. She is the original Skulk. We call her Syrul." See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires
Part 67
Under the Skin 
   The body that once belonged to Heward was finally breaking down. The hair was falling out, and what was left looked like white string. The face was cragged and going crooked, and the spine was bent. Wee Jas hadn't said anything, but Win-Daled the Suel Lich knew that she wasn't attractive to her anymore. Wee Jas was at the Palace less and less.
   It was time for Win-Daled to hunt for a new body. She hated the very thought of taking the life force of another person, but the hunger for life was gnawing away at her her from the inside. Who would she take? The younger and stronger the better, for a young body would last longer, and then she could defer the taking of another for quite some time. 
   A young convict, she decided. Some wastrel who had nothing but hatred in his heart. When she absorbed his life force, his evil would be discarded like a banana peel. She would discuss it with Wee Jas when she next returned. In the meantime, she would take care of herself with lots of sleep.
                               *****
   Win-Daled awoke in a foul mood. She lived down in the depths of the Palace so she had no idea of the time of the night or day. 
   She was hungry.
   That was odd. She seldom ate and taste meant nothing to her in any event. Perhaps her decaying body made her so? She rang for a servant. Wee Jas had several priestesses that lived here under the Palace, serving her small needs. Sworn to secrecy and devoting their lives to the study of meditation and magic, they  knew who and what she was, and revered Win -Daled as a holy companion of their god. Before long, one of the priestesses came into her crypt. She was one of the newer ones, a tall Suel with dark eyes, and her hair was long and braided and almost black. 
   "Yes, Mistress?" Enquired the girl.
   "I wish to eat," said Win-Daled.
   "What shall I bring you, Mistress?"
   Win-Daled didn't know.
   "We have fruits and nuts on hand, Mistress."
   "No."
   "We can prepare a meal for you. Duck or beef, or mutton or fresh fish from the river..."
   Win-Daled turned up her nose.
   "Olve food," she said at last, "bring me elvish food. Grimmleaf stew and toadstool pie. With Celenian wine."
                           *****
   The food had failed to sate her. Win-Daled couldn't taste any of it, and she ended up throwing the dishes at her servant. The priestess didn't flinch, and the half full glass struck her in the face, but she just stood there, letting some blood trickle down.
   "Stupid, clumsy girl," growled Win -Daled, "go away and die.". Win-Daled left her crypt and wandered down a corridor. Where was she going? She wandered around, then headed for the stairs. As she trod up, one of her knees gave way. There was a loud snap as a ligament went.
   Win-Daled crawled back to her room, humiliated and ashamed. Why was she so bad tempered? Why was she hungry...and elvish food? She had never cared for it before. And the poor priestess. She must be very confused. Wasn't Win -Daled usually undemanding and cordial? What was happening to her?
                             ****
   Next time Win-Daled awoke, her knee hadn't healed at all. Her body was deteriorating rapidly now. Her time as Heward had ended. She called for a servant once more. A different woman came this time, an older woman, and one that had served for many years. She was deferential, but Win-Daled couldn't help but see some steel in her blue eyes.
   "Yes Mistress?" said the High Priestess.
   "Where is the girl who served me yesterday?"
   "She is unwell. She rests in the Holy rooms."
  Win-Daled struck her in the mouth. The unnatural chill of Win-Daled's palm singed the woman's cheek. Cold smoke came off her face. The High Priestess gasped, then fell over onto the stone floor.
   Win-Daled was aghast. What had she done that for? Why was she so angry?
   FETCH THE GIRL FOR ME.
   The voice echoed around Win -Daled's skull. What was happening?
   I AM INSIDE YOU. I AM UNDER YOUR SKIN. I REQUIRE A YOUNG AND BEAUTIFUL BODY. I AM THE GITH QUEEN. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 68
Lost in Space 
   Wee Jas and the Star Man hung in space. She didn't need to breathe, for she was only star stuff. Wee Jas didn't need to breathe, but that didn't stop her tears.
   Celestian held her hand. He turned to look at her, his expression concerned. "Wee Jas, are you still sad?"
   It was a spectacular view that they had. Smudges of pink and violet nebulae stretched right around them, and above shone a huge red giant. Celestian always felt cheered up at this point in space. Wee Jas was a good pupil, but she still had more to learn. Celestian disliked her expression of emotion because it meant that she was still too stuck with self identity.
   "Wee Jas," continued Celestian, when Wee Jas hadn't answered, "how can stardust be sad?"
   "Because I am more than stardust. I still live. I am still a person."
   "What is living? What is a person? How do you define a person from a star? Can stars feel sad? If not, why not?"
   "Please, Star Man, you know why not! Aren't you also upset by the way things went?"
   "Many things happen that I don't like. Once they happen they have happened. The cosmos remains."
   "I don't live in the cosmos like you, Celestian, I live in the Suel Imperium. It is all war there now."
   "So you have already told me."
   "What will be will be, you say. Days come and go. Stars shine, explode and become new suns... what's this philosophy done for my life? We did interfere, didn't we? We stopped the githyanki."
   "Some things we can do," said Celestian, ",and some things we can't do."
   "Oh gods! You're impossible to talk to when you are like this. You are cold hearted sometimes!"
   "And sometimes I am not."
   "Star Man, is this all a game to you? You know what happened to me. She is gone!"
   "Win-Daled? Yes..."
   "The Gith Queen took her from me. She took over my Suel Lich and she wrecked the capital...."
   "Yes."
   "Everything I care about is ruined now."
   "But why do you care so much? Oerth is a speck. Oerik is a lump on a speck. The Imperium is a speck on a lump."
   "The Gith Queen destroyed my lover, the skulks joined the goddess of deceit and now no emperor even exists. The Suel Imperium is broken...and you cannot understand...you won't understand..."
   Celestian withdrew his hand that held her. Wee Jas found herself tumbling like a lost leaf, but with no sense of gravity she just spun in place.
   "Let yourself go," urged Celestian, " you are a firebolt. Burn across heaven and be free."
   Wee Jas burst into flames. She was literally an arrow of pure fire. She felt her own heat warm the void itself.
   "That's right, Wee Jas. Fire isn't sad!"
   No, thought Wee Jas, fire is never sad. But it is always angry. See less
